About This Job
The Role
• Understand and build effective and efficient schedules around our clients and Care Professionals.
• Ensure schedules are prepared, considering travel time, holidays, training and last-minute cancellations.
• Be responsive to changes in the schedule and liaise with relevant team members.
• Match Care Professionals to new clients in conjunction with client services team and arrange introductions.
• Ensure client schedules are matched to their needs, with the same Care Professional and the same times each week, where possible.
• Develop excellent relationships with both clients and Care Professionals so both can enjoy positive experiences.
• Work with the recruitment and Managers to ensure sufficient current and future staffing levels are met.
• Work with the Care Team to ensure new and existing care packages can be resourced and scheduled on a timely basis.
• Add and maintain all client and Care Professional information onto to the electronic scheduling system.
• Carry out any other duties deemed necessary for the successful operation of the business.
• Ensure compliance with Home Instead’s Equality, Diversity and Equal Opportunities Policy, in respect of employment and service delivery.
Essential Criteria
• Experience of working in a scheduling role within a home care or other relevant environment such as logistics.
• Good working knowledge of IT systems with experience of Microsoft Office or Google Suite and CRM software with the ability to learn and adopt new technologies where appropriate.
• Highly resilient and positive with excellent communications skills.
• Excellent organisation and prioritisation skills with the ability to work calmly and accurately under pressure.
• Team player with strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build rapport quickly.
• Excellent attention to detail with the ability to multi-task.
• Logical and analytical with the ability to work on own initiative and meet deadlines.

Additional Information
If you have a passion for caring and the motivation to help us achieve our ambitions, we would love to hear from you.
We encourage applications from all sections of the community as we want to reflect the neighbourhoods in which we work. Home Instead is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of adults and expects all staff to share this commitment. This role is subject to DBS enhanced disclosure.

About This Job
Are you looking for a meaningful way to connect with your community?  We have an exciting opportunity for a new care assistant to join our 'Outstanding' island team. If you're looking for some extra weekend or evening work, this could be the perfect position for you!
Where no two visits are the same, daily tasks can include:
Assisting with personal care:
• Provide medication reminders
• Help with bathing, dressing and grooming
• Help with continence care
• Assist to eat and drink
Home help:
• Run errands / collect prescriptions etc
• Performing light housekeeping tasks (dusting, vacuuming, making beds, changing linens, cleaning bathrooms, kitchens, washing and ironing, taking out rubbish, caring for houseplants etc.)
• Organise and tidy cupboards and check food expiry dates
• Plan prepare and tidy away meals
• Answer the door
• Assist with pet care
• Provide Dementia / Alzheimer care
• Provide respite / convalescence care
• Assist with morning/wake up and or evening/tuck in
Companionship:
• Offer companionship and conversation
• Monitor diet and eating
• Stimulate and encourage through a variety of activities (for example clothing selection, hobbies and crafts)
• Arrange and provide reminders for appointments, activities and outings
• Help with travel arrangements
• Organise mail and write letters
• Assist with walking (lending an arm to steady)
• Accompany to appointments and social events (for example visiting friends or family, lunch, club meetings)
Does this sound like the role for you?
Must hold a full UK driving licence

Qualifications
No previous care experience necessary. We are looking for people from across the community who share in our values to provide compassionate care and get to know our clients as you would your own family.

Additional Information
What we provide:
A friendly and relaxed company with an incredibly supportive office and monthly team activities, including care assistant of the month awards.
Competitive pay from £12.50 to £13.50 per hour, with options for  flexible working hours to fit around your lifestyle and commitments.
Fully paid training with our award-winning courses.  In addition, we offer a mentor/ buddy system for the first 12 weeks, continued 24/7 support from our office and regular refresher opportunities and team activities.
Wellness program with access to healthcare and counselling, plus blue light card discount.
Exclusive discounts at high street stores, supermarkets, utility providers and much more.
Contact us today:
Enjoy all of this as part of your new rewarding career with the Home Instead Isle of Wight family.
https://www.homeinstead.co.uk/recruitment/isle-of-wight/

About This Job
Being a Care Professional is a highly rewarding career where no two days are the same! With minimum 1 hour care visits and client matching, you have the time to provide high quality, person-focused care.
Duties can include:
• Companionship - ensuring a client enjoys regular and meaningful social interaction is an important part of your visit
• Help with everyday tasks such as; meal preparation and light housework

About This Job
• Bicycle Repairs: Perform a wide range of bicycle repairs, including but not limited to brake adjustments, gear tuning, wheel truing, drivetrain maintenance, and suspension service. Troubleshoot and diagnose mechanical issues accurately.

• Service Consultations: Interact with customers to assess their bicycle repair and maintenance needs. Provide recommendations and cost estimates for services.

• Safety Inspections: Conduct safety inspections on bicycles to identify and address potential safety hazards.
• Quality Control: Ensure that all repaired bicycles meet the highest quality standards and safety regulations.
• Inventory Management: Maintain a well-organized and efficient workshop, including managing the inventory of spare parts and tools.
• Customer Service: Provide excellent customer service, including explaining repair work to customers, answering questions, and offering advice on bicycle maintenance.

Qualifications
• Proficiency in bicycle mechanics, including the ability to diagnose and repair a wide range of bicycle types and components.
• Previous experience as a bicycle mechanic is highly desirable.
• Knowledge of various bicycle brands, models, and components.
• Strong attention to detail and a commitment to quality workmanship.
• Excellent customer service and communication skills.
• Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
• Knowledge of safety standards and practices related to bicycle repairs.
• Willingness to stay updated on the latest advancements in bicycle technology and repair techniques.
Work is primarily conducted in a workshop environment.
May require standing for extended periods and lifting heavy objects.
Flexible work hours, including weekends and evenings, may be necessary based on the store's operating hours and customer demand.

Full‑time Field & Home‑based Nationwide Travel Required
Adler & Allan is expanding, and we’re looking for a proactive Client Account Manager to take ownership of a portfolio of key strategic accounts. You’ll be responsible for driving growth within a defined set of key accounts—developing tailored account plans, identifying new opportunities, and ensuring every client receives exceptional service. Working closely with Sector Managers, Regional Account Managers and Operational Teams, you’ll bring together commercial insight and operational delivery to strengthen relationships and expand our footprint across each account.
This is a hands‑on, strategic role where you’ll act as the primary day‑to‑day commercial contact, lead customer review meetings, support renewals and negotiations, and ensure accurate forecasting and pipeline management.
What you’ll be doing
• Managing a portfolio of key accounts to achieve revenue, margin and growth targets
• Developing account plans aligned to sector strategy and identifying opportunities and risks
• Building strong relationships with customer stakeholders across multiple functions
• Acting as the main commercial contact for allocated clients
• Creating and maintaining a healthy pipeline with accurate forecasting
• Leading regular customer review meetings and ensuring agreed actions are delivered
• Working with operational teams to ensure service quality and contract compliance
• Supporting renewals, variations and commercial negotiations
• Ensuring pricing accuracy, commercial compliance and correct invoicing
• Managing aged debt and resolving billing queries
• Feeding account insights into sector development plans
• Contributing to tender responses and proposals
• Work & contract winning

Qualifications
What you’ll bring
• Experience in account management or client‑facing commercial roles in B2B services
• Experience with Environmental Consultancy/Services/Engineering
• Strong relationship‑building and communication skills
• Ability to identify opportunities and translate customer needs into solutions
• Solid commercial understanding, including pricing and contract fundamentals
• Excellent planning and organisational skills
• A proactive, solutions‑driven mindset with strong ownership and accountability
• Ability to collaborate effectively across teams
• Confident communicator comfortable engaging with stakeholders at all levels
• Proficiency with CRM systems and Microsoft Office
• Clean UK driving licence and Right to Work in the UK
• Willingness to undergo a Criminal Record Check

Additional Information
Adler and Allan are committed to fostering diversity and inclusion in our workplace. We proudly embrace equal opportunities for all applicants, regardless of race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or national origin. If you require any support with your application, whatever the circumstance, please let us know.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/homeinsteadcare.description_excerpt:
About This Job
Our Care Assistants - who we also proudly call our Care Professionals - support older people to continue living safely, happily and independently in the place they know and love best: their own home. And one of the things that makes Home Instead different is simple: we give you time to care. Our visits are a minimum of one hour, and we focus on matching you with regular clients so you can genuinely get to know the people you support.
You might arrive to help somebody get ready for their day, prepare breakfast and support with medication. Another visit might involve making lunch, heading out for a walk, helping around the home or simply sitting down with a cup of tea and having a proper conversation. Some clients need support with personal care, washing, dressing or mobility. Others may need companionship, meal preparation, medication support or a little help maintaining their independence.
No two clients are the same - and that’s exactly the point. We want care to be personal.
What makes Home Instead different?
There are lots of care jobs out there. We want you to know why we think this one is special...
Minimum one-hour visits
Because brilliant care shouldn't be rushed.
Regular clients
We believe in continuity. Wherever possible, you'll see the same people regularly, giving you the opportunity to build trust and genuine relationships.
Training like you've never known
Our Care Skills Academy is our one-stop shop for growth, knowledge and potential. You'll receive comprehensive, paid training before supporting clients, followed by paid shadowing, mentoring, client-specific training and ongoing development throughout your career with us.
No care experience? That's absolutely fine.
Some of our brilliant Care Professionals came to us having never worked in care before. We'll give you the training, knowledge and support you need - we're much more interested in finding people with the right values, compassion and attitude.
A team behind you
Working in the community doesn't mean working alone. You'll have ongoing support from our office team, opportunities to meet other Care Professionals and people to turn to when you need advice, reassurance or simply a friendly voice.
A career if you want one
For some people, becoming a Care Assistant is the perfect job to fit around other commitments. For others, it's the beginning of an entirely new career. We offer clear development pathways, funded qualifications, apprenticeships and opportunities to progress.

Additional Information
And yes, the practical stuff matters too!
You'll receive:
• £13.05 per hour Monday to Friday
• £13.80 per hour at weekends
• £26.10 per hour on bank holidays
• Paid mileage and travel time between client visits
• Full paid training through our Care Skills Academy
• Support to achieve your Care Certificate
• Career development opportunities and funded qualifications, including NVQs and apprenticeships
• Workplace pension and holiday pay
• Access to your pay before payday through our PayWise+ app
• Free Blue Light Card
• Access to discounted fuel
• Referral rewards for helping us grow our team and client community
• Ongoing support from a friendly, close-knit team
• Regular opportunities to meet and connect with other Care Professionals
Who are we looking for?
We're not looking for one particular type of person. You might already be an experienced Care Assistant looking for a provider that gives you more time with your clients. You might work in retail, hospitality, childcare, customer service or an entirely different industry and be wondering whether care could be for you. You might be returning to work, looking for something more meaningful, or simply ready for a change.
What matters to us is who you are.
We're looking for people who are warm, compassionate and reliable. People who turn up when they say they will, take pride in doing things properly and understand just how important they can become in somebody else's life. You don't need to know everything about care on day one. That's our job to teach you.
When can I work?
We have a variety of hours available and will talk to you about what could work alongside your other commitments. We have a current need for full-time Care Professionals living in the Vale of White Horse to support clients around Faringdon, Shrivenham, Highworth, Wantage and surrounding villages. Our busiest times are mornings and evenings, so some capacity to work a mixture of these is helpful. We also work alternate weekends, so you must be able to commit to that. We would be interested in speaking to anyone looking for part-time hours also.
You'll supporting clients home to home, so being comfortable travelling locally is important. Due to the community-based nature of the role, a full driving licence and access to a vehicle is required.
You must also be aged 18 or over.
A job that feels like more than a job
There aren't many jobs where making somebody a meal, taking the time to listen to a story, helping someone feel confident enough to leave the house, or simply arriving at the door with a familiar smile can completely change somebody's day. For our clients and their families, the right Care Professional can mean reassurance, companionship, confidence and the ability to remain living at home. For you, it can mean going home knowing your work genuinely mattered.
We're incredibly proud of the care our team provides, and we're looking for more brilliant people to join us. So, if you're looking for a job with purpose, proper training, great relationships and a team that genuinely cares about doing things well, we'd love to hear from you.
So, is care your calling? Apply today and come and find out what being a Home Instead Care Professional could mean for you.
Please note: This is a UK-based role and any offer of employment is subject to candidates having the right to work in the UK. We do not offer visa sponsorship.

Other benefits

• A paid volunteering day each year.
• Ongoing training, development and clear career pathways.
• 25 days’ holiday (rising to 27 with service) with the option to buy more up to 5 days.
What you’ll do in this role:
• Conduct functional assessments which include initial reviews, face-to-face, video or telephone assessments to evaluate how a claimant’s health condition or disability affects them for various types of benefit.
• Analyse and interpret clinical information and supporting evidence.
• Write detailed evidence-based reports to support the DWP/DfC in making informed and objective decisions - no treatment or diagnosis required.
• Use IT systems to support clinical decision-making and report writing.
• Develop your clinical knowledge and constantly learn about health conditions which are less familiar to you.
What are PIP and WCA?
• Personal Independence Payment (PIP) is a benefit for people with a long-term health condition or impairment. It is paid to make a contribution to the extra costs that disabled people may face, to help them lead full, active and independent lives.
• Work Capability Assessment (WCA) is a functional assessment that looks at a range of different activities relating to physical, mental, intellectual and cognitive functions, to help DWP determine a customer's capability for work or work-related activity.

Qualifications
About you
•
Registered Nurse (RGN, RCN, RMN or RNLD), Paramedic, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist, or Pharmacist
•
Full registration with a relevant UK regulatory body (NMC, HCPC,  GPhC or equivalent), with an active PIN and no restrictions.
•
At least one year of broad post-registration clinical experience working with adult patients
•
Excellent observational, questioning and communication skills, giving you the ability to listen, empathise and dig deeper
•
Ability to produce clear, accurate and detailed reports from multiple information sources
•
Comfortable and able to work quickly to meet structured targets
•
Good IT skills including experience using clinical IT systems, Microsoft Office, and the ability to learn and utilise new systems effectively.
Please note: all candidates must hold the right to work in the UK as we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

We were awarded two contracts to deliver the Health Assessment Advisory Service (HAAS) assessments in the Midlands and Wales for the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), and in Northern Ireland for the Department for Communities (DfC).
We deliver assessments for a variety of different benefits, including delivering PIP, WCA and Specialist benefit assessments across the Midlands and Wales, and in Northern Ireland.

•
SKILLS:

We have a radically transparent and kind team culture. To say people at our clients business are passionate about our mission is not PR bull, we all very much care about helping parents reintegrate into the workplace (especially mums) and about improving the face of child development.

We all want to create a compelling and beautiful experience, but we all favour progress over perfection. The sorts of problems you’ll be tasked with solving are: – How do we help families and nannies communicate better – How do we ensure we’re making perfect family/nanny matches (like digital dating matching algorithms) – What’s the best way to profoundly impact the well-being of all families We hope you’ll agree, these aren’t your run-of-the mill tech problems.
About you
You consistently put both users and data before your ego. You have lots to teach others about the value of design, and are equally willing to learn from those around you. You welcome and give honest feedback, especially when it’s hard to do. Must have: – Authenticity. We want you to be you, not the “work” version of you – Extremely good critical thinking – Experience working with Design Systems and Pattern Libraries, ideally having lead their development – Experience designing for native & web products – Degree in a human behaviour or computer science related field, or equivalent practical experience – 4+ years of relevant work experience as a UX/Product Designer in a product environment –
The ability to gain appropriate feedback from users on your solutions through qualitative and quantitative testing – Strong abilities to turn user research into solutions, with Information Architecture, Interface Design and Interaction Design in your toolkit – Confidence in articulating the strengths and limitations of various design approaches –
Opinions on what makes for good/bad design for a given problem – An analytical mind that uses empirical data as well as opinions to back up your arguments and fight your cause – Emotional intelligence – High level of creativity and problem solving skills – You must be nice What we’d love you to have (you should have about ? of the below): –
Experience working in an Agile/Lean environment with rapid prototyping and iterative development – A solid understanding of a broad set of qualitative and quantitative research methods, and strong understanding of experiment design principles –
An analytical mind that uses empirical evidence as well as opinions to back up your arguments and fight your cause – Ability to reason by first principles –
A level of expertise that excites and scares us together with the desire to share your expertise – Excellent writing skills – The confidence to influence, share and collaborate early on in the design process – The ability to do more with less. The desire to look for simpler but better solutions. – A Brobdingnagian passion & belief in your own ideas but the humility to recognise when you’re wrong – An understanding of the pros and cons of Lean – You’re a “Manager of One” – The ability to do more with less.
The desire to look for simpler but better solutions If we had to sum it up in three words, they’d be “Smart, Kind, Creative”. Facilitate workshops, Design Sprints, and Design Studios as needed – and be a protagonist for iterative design and development How you’ll be measured Ultimately, it comes down to three things, in order of importance: – Your impact on our mission – The quality of output

About This Job
Due to increased opportunities and demand in the Energy & Natural Resources division, the Energy & Natural Resources team are recruiting a Senior Project Planner to join a diverse and supportive team during a period of significant growth. Our nuclear client is at the forefront of industry leading change, and we are keen to speak to individuals with project planning experience to see what Turner & Townsend can offer you. Candidates will be required to be present in our client office for 3 days per week.
MAIN PURPOSE OF ROLE
A Planner will be responsible for work packages and projects of varying size and complexity. Due to the nature of the programme of works, work packages may vary in size with Planners accountable for scheduling multiple smaller projects or one which could be significantly larger in value. A Planner will be responsible for taking the lead on planning for multiple non-related projects or single highly complex projects within the programme of works. They will understand and manage relationships between time, cost, risk, change, reporting and scope, with accountability for creating and maintaining robust schedules that provide our clients with accurate data to drive management decisions. They will play a key role in ensuring that client objectives are met and that projects are delivered to time and cost targets and the appropriate quality standards.
KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES
• As a Planner, you have a passion to provide services as required by our clients, which may include:
• Taking the lead on planning, supporting more junior planning professionals on novel, high value projects or programmes.
• Creation, development and maintenance of project schedules that assist and align with project requirements on a complex, risk managed project or programme.
• Adherence to NEC or FIDIC contract processes for management of schedule data and submissions.
• Assisting the project team to develop status reports to keep management informed on project progress.
• Involvement with senior team in oversight of day-to-day management, staffing and the implementation of Integrated Project Controls standards and processes.
• Reducing uncertainty, improving efficiency and understanding project objectives.
• Interacting with the project team to define scope of work to develop and update detailed schedules, cost information and identification of variances from original schedule.
• Assisting project managers to schedule work and coordinate assignments.
• Evaluation of project schedule progress and performance and identify developing problem areas.
• Analysis of float, critical path and constraints to understand the effect of approved changes or slippages to schedule, recommending alternative courses of action for recovery.
• Undertaking project progress reviews.
• Monitoring and consolidation of multiple project schedules into Integrated master Schedule (IMS).
• Monitoring the project managers reporting system summarising the progress status of all projects.
• Monitor and advise on status of project KPIs across multiple projects.
• Understand and report EVM on a periodic basis.
• Functional management of planning personnel within the Turner & Townsend team, conducting mentoring and coaching as required.

Qualifications
You have professional Project Controls experience specialising in Planning & Scheduling in one or more sectors across the whole Project lifecycle. While nuclear experience is desirable it is not an absolute requirement. You have strong knowledge and proficiency with Primavera (P6) and other planning and resourcing software and can coordinate and work with other teams utilising your multi-disciplinary knowledge.
You will be a strong communicator, able to demonstrate leadership behaviours with the ability to influence, manage, motivate, coach and develop a team by fostering a diverse and inclusive environment. You promote empowerment and contribution and have a passion to build a community and support network beyond your delivery role.
You also;
• Will be able to obtain BPSS level security clearance.

About This Job
In Custody Careers Advisor (CIAG)
Salary:  £27,800
Location: HMP Kirklevington Grange
We’re looking for a dedicated Careers Information Advice and Guidance Advisor to join our team - a crucial role in supporting individuals inside a custodial setting by providing tailored career advice, guidance, and support. This role aims to empower prisoners to identify their career aspirations, develop their skills, and leverage their strengths to prepare for successful reintegration into society upon release.
About the Role:
You will provide tailored careers advice and guidance to prisoners through both one-to-one sessions and group workshops. You will create and manage personalised learning plans to help prisoners to identify and work towards their goals during custody and in preparation for release. Your role will support rehabilitation by equipping individuals with the skills, qualifications, and opportunities needed to secure employment or further training upon release.
You will organise opportunities for prisoners to connect with employers and participate in employment related activities. Through your support, prisoners will be encouraged to take meaningful steps towards long-term career development and positive reintegration into the community.
This is a demanding yet deeply rewarding role. You'll be working in a challenging environment with individuals who have complex needs and may be hesitant to engage. However, when you help someone break the cycle and take real steps towards transforming their life, the impact is truly life-changing—for them and for you.
What You'll Be Doing:
• Caseload management: Conduct one-to-one assessments to identify prisoners’ skills, career aspirations and training needs and develop a Prisoner Learning Plan (PLP) and effectively manage your caseload to achieve sustained employment, training, education and completion of prison employment outcomes.
• Facilitation: Delivery of engaging sessions to groups of participants around topics such as employability skills, career planning and effective disclosure. Ensuring that goals are realistic and consider any barriers to employment sectors due to the nature of certain types of convictions.
• Relationship Building: Foster genuine, trusting, and non-judgemental relationships with participants creating a safe space for personal growth.
• Stakeholder management: Engage with prison education departments, training providers, employers and probation services to create employment pathways.
• Quality Recording: Work towards agreed KPIs, targets, ensuring quality assurance standards in accordance with the service provider are met.

Qualifications

• Experience delivering guidance, support or advisory services to individuals
• Ability to assess individual needs and develop action plans to support progression

• Experience of working with individuals facing barriers to employment or education

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/wise/7440001552.description_excerpt:
About This Job
The role
We’re looking for a Senior Product Analytics Manager to set the strategic direction for analytics in our Global Send Experience Squad. You’ll help the squad decide where to focus, which customer problems to solve and how Wise can grow its global money transfer business, which today drives 5% of all cross-border transfers in the world for personal customers.
You’ll work closely with Product, Design and Engineering to lead discovery across the remittance space: building a deep understanding of customer needs, finding the biggest opportunities and turning them into a clear product strategy. You’ll influence decisions across the factors that shape whether customers choose to send money with Wise—including price, speed and convenience—throughout the whole customer lifecycle, from a customer’s first transfer to the choices they make as a returning customer.
You’ll lead a group of senior analysts. Your focus will be on setting the team’s direction and helping the squad make its most important strategic decisions. You’ll coach analysts to partner closely with teams on day-to-day product questions, while staying hands-on with the most complex and consequential opportunities yourself.
You’ll help us answer questions such as:
•
Where are the biggest opportunities to grow money transfers around the world?
•
What matters most to customers when they decide where, when and how to send money?
•
How do price, speed and convenience shape customers’ choices and behaviour?
•
How could an AI-powered concierge help customers find and complete the right transfer, while making the experience simpler and more personal?
•
How can we make the experience work better for both new and returning customers?
•
Which customer problems should we solve to make the biggest difference to growth and customer value?
•
How should we focus our product strategy to grow our money transfer revenues 10x over the next few years?
What you’ll be doing
•
Set the strategic direction for the squad. Partner with Product, Design and Engineering to build a clear view of customer needs, market opportunities and the choices Wise should make next.
•
Lead discovery and opportunity finding. Explore customer behaviour and the end-to-end transfer journey to identify unmet needs, friction and growth opportunities. Help the squad understand not just what is happening, but where it has the greatest opportunity to act.
•
Influence the whole customer decision. Bring an analytical perspective to how customers weigh price, speed and convenience when choosing how to send money, across both new and returning customer journeys.
•
Turn opportunities into product priorities. Size customer and commercial opportunities, develop clear points of view and help teams make focused, evidence-based choices about what to build and why.
•
Lead and develop a group of senior analysts. Set a high bar for analytical thinking and impact, coach analysts in their work and careers, and create the conditions for them to support their teams effectively.
•
Enable strong day-to-day squad decisions. Coach analysts to work closely with their product teams, bring useful insights into planning and discovery, and help teams learn from product changes and customer behaviour.
•
Stay hands-on with the most important problems. Work directly on high-impact or ambiguous questions, and guide the team through complex analysis when the strategic stakes are high.
•
Bring people together around a shared view. Communicate complex evidence clearly, influence senior stakeholders and help cross-functional teams turn strategic choices into action.

Qualifications
What you’ll bring
•
Experience leading and developing strong analytics teams, including experienced or senior analysts.
•
A track record of shaping product strategy and business direction through analytics.
•
Strong product and commercial judgement: you can connect customer needs, product choices, growth and sustainable economics.
•
Experience leading discovery and identifying high-value opportunities in ambiguous problem spaces.
•
A deep understanding of product analytics and customer behaviour across acquisition, conversion and retention.
•
Expertise in using quantitative evidence—including experimentation and causal analysis—to inform decisions, while knowing when the most valuable contribution is defining the right problem or opportunity.
•
Strong technical analytical skills, including SQL, and the ability to guide reliable, high-quality analytics.
•
Excellent communication skills: you can make complex ideas clear, form a point of view and bring people with you.
•
The ability to set long-term direction while staying close enough to the work to help teams make progress.
•
An interest in international payments and the needs of people sending money across borders.

About This Job
About us:
Applications are invited for the role of Head of Hard FM within the Estates Department of the University of the West of England.
Based at our Frenchay campus but covering the entire university estate (predominantly the Bristol area), you will be responsible for all aspects of hard FM for all university properties.
As a member of the Estates senior management team, the successful applicant will lead and manage professional services, support strategic planning and in order to support the efficient managing of the university estate be responsible for operational delivery for all major and specialist contracts and operations.
This post will develop and manage systems of work for sourcing, specifying and scheduling planned and reactive maintenance across the University estate. The post holder manages capital projects linked to the Estates Capital Maintenance (ECM) Plan.
About you:
The skills and experience required for this post are; leadership and operational management of the Hard FM Services (HFMS) team, ability to deliver effective and efficient use of allocated resources, including staffing and R&M and ECM budgets, an effective communicator acting as the key liaison point for the HFMS team with other services and faculties, and a keen facilitator of collaborative working and developing the service.
Furthermore, lead and contribute to University wide projects, developing and promoting innovative thinking and being a strategic thinker to contribute to the development of University policies and procedures in line with service strategy and plans.
About UWE Bristol:
We are one of the largest providers of Higher Education in the South West with over 30,000 students, 250,000 alumni and 3,800 staff. We are both globally connected and regionally embedded, with strong employer and partner connections. Our staff and students come from over 160 countries making this a diverse, dynamic and rewarding place to work and study.
We are an ambitious university. Together, our people are working hard to advance knowledge, inspire people and transform futures. We are looking for people with the skills and ambition to help us achieve those aims.
We have a lot to be proud of at UWE, our achievements include an impressive 88% overall student satisfaction in the most recent National Student Satisfaction survey, placing us 2nd of all universities in England and 7th in the UK. We are 6th in the UK for postgraduate student satisfaction (Postgraduate Taught Experience Survey) and importantly, 96% of UWE Bristol graduates are in employment or further study within six months after graduation. We have also achieved TEF Gold status, have been ranked 21st in The Guardian Best UK Universities 2021 and 29th in the latest Times Higher Education 'Table of Tables'.
This post is based at our lively Frenchay campus where we have invested in the latest facilities and resources to give both our staff and students access to everything they need to succeed – with £300m having been invested recently on new state-of-the-art learning spaces and accommodation while incredible new facilities continue to be developed to enhance our offer even further.
Frenchay campus has excellent transport links; as well as being located near the motorway network we are within walking distance of two train stations, our bus terminus connects us to the local bus and metrobus network and we also have a range of cycling and changing facilities, making our campus the ideal place to work for those commuting to Bristol.
In addition to progressive pay rates, UWE Bristol offers a wide range of employee benefits including:
• a generous holiday allowance of 27 days
• up to 12.5 bank holiday/closure days per year
• flexible working
• excellent defined benefit pension schemes
• access to employee assistance programme
• ongoing learning and development opportunities
• family friendly policies and wellbeing initiatives
• onsite nursery at our Frenchay Campus.
• savings on purchases via Wider Wallet scheme
• option to participate in the cycle to work scheme
Further information
This is a permanent post, and is full-time working 37 hours per week. This post is not available on a jobshare basis.
We particularly encourage applications from BAME applicants as we are currently under represented in these areas - although all appointments will be made on merit.
The University’s normal practice is that new appointments will be made at the starting point of the grade.
UWE is committed to supporting and promoting equality and diversity to create an inclusive working environment. We believe this can be achieved through attracting, developing, and retaining a diverse range of staff from many different backgrounds who share our ambition to be a university recognised for the success and impact of our practice-oriented programmes; our strong industry networks and our inclusive global outlook.
We are able to sponsor qualifying candidates for this role under the Home Office Skilled Worker visa route. Please read our Skilled Worker Guidance to assess if you will be eligible to be sponsored under the criteria.
Please also refer to the Home Office Right to Work Checklist which provides details of which documents are acceptable to prove your right to work in the UK. Should you be shortlisted you will be asked to produce your right to work documents at your interview.

Our Deputy Managers are brilliant retail leaders, accountable for the day to day running of our stores in the absence of the Store Manager.

Location: Melsonby
What you'll do
As a CAD Design Engineer, you will be responsible for producing and maintaining detailed 3D CAD models, manufacturing drawings, and engineering documentation using Autodesk Inventor. Working closely with Electrical Design Engineers and cross-functional teams, you will ensure designs are accurate, manufacturable, and delivered to project timescales.
Your responsibilities will include:
• Creating detailed 3D CAD models and engineering drawings using Autodesk Inventor.
• Producing manufacturing drawings, fabrication drawings, assembly drawings and complete drawing packages.
• Creating and maintaining Bills of Materials (BOMs).
• Carrying out structural analysis using FEA simulations.
• Developing and programming iLogic functions and other design automation tools.
• Working with Autodesk Vault to manage product data and version control.
• Collaborating with Electrical Design Engineers to deliver complete design packages.
• Producing drawing sets for product approvals and supporting project model reviews.
• Maintaining CAD document archives and supporting project close-out activities.
• Identifying opportunities for continuous improvement across design processes and documentation.
• Supporting production by preparing production packs and assisting with large-scale engineering projects.
What we're looking for
You'll be a motivated and detail-oriented engineer who enjoys solving technical challenges and working collaboratively with colleagues across engineering, manufacturing and production. You'll be able to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines and maintain a high standard of accuracy in everything you produce.

Qualifications

Essential
• HNC or HND in Engineering or a relevant discipline.
• A minimum of 5 years' experience in a CAD Design role within an engineering or manufacturing environment.
• At least 3 years' experience using Autodesk Inventor.
• Experience producing manufacturing drawings and applying Design for Manufacture (DFM) principles.
• Experience managing Bills of Materials and CAD data through ERP/PDM systems.
• Strong working knowledge of Autodesk Vault Professional.
• Experience producing assembly drawings, fabrication drawings, layouts and detailed component drawings.
• Excellent understanding of manufacturing processes, materials, tolerances and design constraints.
• Extensive experience using and programming Autodesk iLogic and other CAD automation functions.
• Strong attention to detail with excellent organisational and time management skills.
• Effective communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively across multiple departments.
• Full UK Driving Licence.
• Right to work in the UK.
Desirable
• Experience carrying out Finite Element Analysis (FEA).
• Knowledge of structural design principles.
• Experience supporting product lifecycle management processes.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/homeinsteadcare.description_excerpt:
About This Job
Our Care Assistants - who we also proudly call our Care Professionals - support older people to continue living safely, happily and independently in the place they know and love best: their own home. And one of the things that makes Home Instead different is simple: we give you time to care. Our visits are a minimum of one hour, and we focus on matching you with regular clients so you can genuinely get to know the people you support.
You might arrive to help somebody get ready for their day, prepare breakfast and support with medication. Another visit might involve making lunch, heading out for a walk, helping around the home or simply sitting down with a cup of tea and having a proper conversation. Some clients need support with personal care, washing, dressing or mobility. Others may need companionship, meal preparation, medication support or a little help maintaining their independence.
No two clients are the same - and that’s exactly the point. We want care to be personal.

Additional Information
What makes Home Instead different?
There are lots of care jobs out there. We want you to know why we think this one is special.
Minimum one-hour visits
Because brilliant care shouldn't be rushed.
Contracted hours
We know people like certainty and reliability with their income, so hours with us can be contracted.
Regular clients
We believe in continuity. Wherever possible, you'll see the same people regularly, giving you the opportunity to build trust and genuine relationships.
Training like you've never known
Our Care Skills Academy is our one-stop shop for growth, knowledge and potential. You'll receive comprehensive, paid training before supporting clients, followed by shadowing, mentoring, client-specific training and ongoing development throughout your career with us.
No care experience? That's absolutely fine.
Some of our brilliant Care Professionals came to us having never worked in care before. We'll give you the training, knowledge and support you need - we're much more interested in finding people with the right values, compassion and attitude.
A team behind you
Working in the community doesn't mean working alone. You'll have ongoing support from our office team, opportunities to meet other Care Professionals and people to turn to when you need advice, reassurance or simply a friendly voice.
A career if you want one
For some people, becoming a Care Assistant is the perfect job to fit around other commitments. For others, it's the beginning of an entirely new career. We offer clear development pathways, funded qualifications and opportunities to progress.
And yes, the practical stuff matters too!
You'll receive:
• £13.45 per hour Monday to Friday
• £14.20 per hour at weekends
• £26.90 per hour on bank holidays
• Contracted hours, if desired
• Paid mileage and travel time between client visits
• Full paid training through our Care Skills Academy
• Support to achieve your Care Certificate
• Career development opportunities and funded qualifications, including NVQs and apprenticeships
• Workplace pension and holiday pay
• Access to your pay before payday
• Free Blue Light Card
• Access to discounted fuel
• Referral rewards for helping us grow our team and client community
• Ongoing support from a friendly, close-knit team
• Regular opportunities to meet and connect with other Care Professionals
Who are we looking for?
We're not looking for one particular type of person. You might already be an experienced Care Assistant looking for a provider that gives you more time with your clients. You might work in retail, hospitality, childcare, customer service or an entirely different industry and be wondering whether care could be for you. You might be returning to work, looking for something more meaningful, or simply ready for a change.
What matters to us is who you are.
We're looking for people who are warm, compassionate and reliable. People who turn up when they say they will, take pride in doing things properly and understand just how important they can become in somebody else's life.
You don't need to know everything about care on day one. That's our job to teach you.
When can I work?
We have a variety of hours available and will talk to you about what could work alongside your other commitments. It could be full-time or part-time. Our clients need us seven days a week, so we do ask our Care Professionals to work alternate weekends, covering both Saturday and Sunday, with hours that match what you usually do during the week. Mornings and evenings are busy for us, so if you can cover some of these, that'd be ideal.
You'll primarily be supporting clients across Witney, Carterton, Burford and the surrounding villages, so being comfortable travelling locally is important. Due to the community-based nature of the role, a full driving licence and access to a vehicle is required.
You must also be aged 18 or over.
A job that feels like more than a job
There aren't many jobs where making somebody breakfast, taking the time to listen to a story, helping someone feel confident enough to leave the house, or simply arriving at the door with a familiar smile can completely change somebody's day. For our clients and their families, the right Care Professional can mean reassurance, companionship, confidence and the ability to remain living at home. For you, it can mean going home knowing your work genuinely mattered.
We're incredibly proud of the care our team provides, and we're looking for more brilliant people to join us. So, if you're looking for a job with purpose, proper training, great relationships and a team that genuinely cares about doing things well, we'd love to hear from you.
So, is care your calling? Apply today and come and find out what being a Home Instead Care Professional could mean for you.
Please note: This is a UK-based role and any offer of employment is subject to candidates having the right to work in the UK. We do not offer visa sponsorship.

About This Job
Our functional specialists write reports which help the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) make important decisions about a person’s health and care.
Maybe you’re a nurse right now and you’d like to move away from direct care - this role offers you the chance to not only improve your assessment skills, but also to use your knowledge and experience to make important clinical recommendations. Or you might be an occupational therapist, physiotherapist or paramedic wanting to learn how to evaluate situations in a different way in a different setting. We’re looking for people with the compassion and experience to understand our claimants’ health conditions/disabilities and how they impact their lives.
This role is different from other healthcare professions, and that’s why we take your training and development seriously. You’ll receive comprehensive training with time set aside for self-development learning.
If you’re looking for a change, including more regular working hours, a competitive salary and are ready to expand your skills and experience, this could be the role for you.
What you’ll do in this role:
• Conduct functional assessments which include initial reviews, face-to-face, video or telephone assessments to evaluate how a claimant’s health condition or disability affects them for various types of benefit.
• Analyse and interpret clinical information and supporting evidence.
• Write detailed evidence-based reports to support the DWP/DfC in making informed and objective decisions - no treatment or diagnosis required.
• Use IT systems to support clinical decision-making and report writing.
• Develop your clinical knowledge and constantly learn about health conditions which are less familiar to you.
• This role will deliver mainly face-to-face assessments.
What are PIP and WCA?
• Personal Independence Payment (PIP) is a benefit for people with a long-term health condition or impairment. It is paid to make a contribution to the extra costs that disabled people may face, to help them lead full, active and independent lives.
• Work Capability Assessment (WCA) is a functional assessment that looks at a range of different activities relating to physical, mental, intellectual and cognitive functions, to help DWP determine a customer's capability for work or work-related activity.

Qualifications

•
Registered Nurse (RGN, RCN, RMN or RNLD), Paramedic, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist, or Pharmacist

Full registration with a relevant UK regulatory body (NMC, HCPC, GPhC or equivalent), with an active PIN and no restrictions.
•
At least one year of broad post-registration clinical experience working with adult patients

Excellent observational, questioning and communication skills, giving you the ability to listen, empathise and dig deeper

Ability to produce clear, accurate and detailed reports from multiple information sources
•
Comfortable and able to work quickly to meet structured targets

Good IT skills including experience using clinical IT systems, Microsoft Office, and the ability to learn and utilise new systems effectively.

At vetting, you will undergo an enhanced criminality check which will show both spent and unspent convictions.

Additional Information

You’ll be contracted to work 7.5 hours per day, 37.5 hours per week (full time).  Part time options are also available - 3 days (22.5 hours) or 4 days (30 hours) per week.
Please note, due to business needs, part-time staff will be required to work on a Friday each week as part of their usual pattern. Also there will be an initial full time (paid) training period of 8 weeks so candidates must be able to commit to that.
Please note for part-time roles the initial training period of 8 weeks (paid) is full time so candidate must be able to commit to that.

Join Us in Shaping the Future of Shipbuilding
At Navantia UK, we are delivering some of the most ambitious shipbuilding and heavy-engineering projects in the country. We are looking for a talented Structural Weights & Lifting Engineer to join our Production Engineering team in Belfast and help ensure that every major lift, turn and movement of critical structures is executed safely, efficiently and with engineering excellence.
This is an exciting opportunity to work at the heart of large-scale marine and defence programmes—where your expertise will directly influence production performance, operational safety and project success.
About the Role
As a  Weights & Lifting Structural Engineer, you will be the technical authority for all lifting and turning operations across the shipyard. You’ll apply engineering analysis, modelling and strong problem-solving skills to develop safe, practical and cost-effective lifting plans and methodologies.
You will collaborate closely with production teams, clients and third-party specialists, ensuring that every operation meets rigorous industry standards and reflects best practice. You’ll also play a hands-on role by attending key lifts on-site to confirm compliance and continuously improve our engineering processes.
Key Responsibilities:
• Produce detailed calculations, analyses, drawings and documentation for safe heavy lifting and turning operations.
• Develop lifting plans and reports to support work packages and project design books.
• Assess lifting requirements against yard capabilities, lifting equipment inventory and industry good practice.
• Maintain forward planning for workload, deadlines and resource needs, in collaboration with the Production Engineering Manager.
• Deliver solutions that are safe, cost-effective and fit for purpose.
• Maintain an electronic database of lifting arrangements and documentation.
• Engage with clients, attend site visits and participate in reviews as required.
• Support operational teams during execution of lift activities and provide expert guidance on best lifting practices.
• Keep up to date with relevant standards, legislation and regulations (BS, API, DCR, HS&E, EU directives).
• Review the implementation of your lifting designs on-site and feed lessons learned back into future designs.

Personal Independence Payment (PIP) is a benefit for people with a long-term health condition or impairment. It is paid to make a contribution to the extra costs that disabled people may face, to help them lead full, active and independent lives.
•
Work Capability Assessment (WCA) is a functional assessment that looks at a range of different activities relating to physical, mental, intellectual and cognitive functions, to help DWP/DfC determine a customer's capability for work or work-related activity.

Projects include commercial buildings like 80 – 100 Victoria Street London, British Library, multiple residential buildings in the Royal Borough of Greenwich and even Windsor Castle.

• Data Centres: Working for multiple major hyperscale projects in the Nordics, Iberia and South America. These projects provide the opportunity to tackle the issue of data management and storage specific to each country. Designing and implementing a highly resilient electrical infrastructure entails the usage of an efficient system that is highly sustainable.
• Lansdowne House: High-end commercial office development occupying the South-East side of Berkley Square, Mayfair, City of Westminster, with an all- electric energy centre containing Ground Source Heat Pumps, Air Source Heat Pumps and High Efficiency Chillers.

The team is seeking to expand their capabilities further by adding a Senior Public Health Engineer with experience in delivering sustainable projects across multiple sectors, has excellent team working and co-ordination skills and strives for technical excellence.
You will be an integral part of the diverse and dynamic national AECOM PH team which will support your technical career development. Challenges such as the net zero agenda and water neutrality provide great opportunities for your career to flourish with the role also including Fire Protection systems design which will be supported by our experienced specialist fire protection engineering team to provide the opportunity to develop new design skills. The position is predominantly office located role to ensure face-to-face contact time with the team.
The Senior Engineer will be responsible for leading much of the Public Health and Fire Protection systems design on projects and involve client liaison, mentoring and leading the discipline/systems to prepare scheme and detailed engineering designs. The successful candidate will have proven design experience, delivering to quality, time and budget. This role will suit someone with who is enthusiastic, self-motivated, and looking to advance their career.
The role will include taking point lead on multiple PH systems design/calculations on a project as well as assisting the lead PH engineer with experience in the following systems:
• Hot and cold water systems
• Above ground foul and rainwater system
• Fire Protection Systems
• Below Ground drainage systems
• Pumped drainage systems
• Water and oil leak detection systems
• Rainwater harvesting and Greywater recycling systems
• Water conservation solutions
• BREEAM, LEED and Ska Rating design integration
Duties of the role will include, but not be limited to;
• Maintaining Client relationships
• Mentoring and developing staff
• Project Managing small sized multi-disciplinary projects
• Obtain the necessary information both internally and externally from Architects, Quantity Surveyors and Design Consultants to provide a fully coordinated design
• Ensure the Design Team is kept fully informed of all technical and other information necessary for the duration of the project
• Be familiar with the BIM design process and be capable of input and support for projects designed in Revit
• Ensure compliance with all Statutory and Regulatory obligations, make submissions to the Statutory Authorities and obtain approvals as necessary
• Produce all design information and ensure that all calculations are prepared and signed off in accordance with the requirements of the QA procedures, relevant Standards and Codes of Practice
• Represent AECOM at Client, Design Team and Progress meetings throughout the design and construction phases of projects
• Support AECOM PM with input to pre-qualification and selection of contractors, also respond to tender queries, comment and review tender returns
• Ensure the project work complies with the Project Management Plan and Programme
• Understand and implement AECOM’s Safety Health and Environment Policy
Minimum Requirements:
• Previous public health engineering work experience within design consultancy or other relevant business
• A comprehensive working knowledge of statutory regulations to ensure design compliance, make submissions to the statutory authorities and obtaining approvals as necessary
• Be able to work independently and have good time/task management skills
• Experience in mixed used, residential, commercial and healthcare buildings/sectors
• Fully competent in the use of AutoCad to produce 2D drawings
• Fully competence in using 3D Revit software and Navisworks reviewing software
• Ability to speak fluently and communicate effectively in written reports and oral presentations

About This Job
Role Purpose
The role purpose is to support the entrepreneurial syndication and distribution of credit facilities originated across the Bank’s client franchise, helping to broaden the Bank’s investor base across banks, development finance institutions, credit insurers and wider institutional capital providers. Integrated within the Lending business unit, the role works closely with origination, structuring, coverage and control functions to shape fundable and distributable transactions, mobilise third-party capital, improve portfolio and capital efficiency, and support the Bank’s growth strategy across trade finance, structured finance and commodity finance.
Role Responsibilities
•
Broaden and deepen the Bank’s distribution and investor network across banks, non-bank financial institutions, development finance institutions, credit insurers, private credit and private equity credit funds, fixed-income and emerging-market debt funds, asset managers, family offices, insurance investors and other institutional capital providers.
•
Develop and maintain a detailed investor appetite and market-intelligence framework, ensuring likely funding sources are identified early and that investor requirements inform transaction development, pricing, structuring and marketing.
•
Execute distribution strategies for trade-finance assets and facilities on a funded and unfunded basis, including the preparation and coordination of transaction summaries, teasers, information memoranda, investor presentations, data rooms and other marketing materials.
•
Act as a subject-matter expert for the placement of structured finance and commodity finance risk, assessing distributability and marketability across cash flows, collateral, borrowing-base mechanics, security arrangements, credit enhancement, repayment sources and other relevant risk mitigants.
•
Work with Origination, Structuring and Coverage to convert opportunities into fundable, executable and investor-ready transactions, including commodity finance, structured credit, portfolio solutions, risk-sharing structures and other transactions designed to mobilise institutional capital.
•
Identify and structure appropriate combinations of bank funding, institutional capital, development finance and credit insurance to support transactions requiring multiple sources of risk capacity.
•
Manage syndication opportunities end to end, including opportunity assessment, syndication strategy, client pitches, approval materials, syndicate formation, investor engagement, documentation, execution, financial close and any post-closing sell-down.
•
Coordinate lender and investor communications throughout syndication and distribution processes, ensuring consistent, accurate and timely information is provided and that confidentiality, due diligence, pricing, allocation and closing processes are managed effectively.
•
Collaborate with Coverage, Product, Credit, Risk, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Finance and other stakeholders to identify opportunities early, support cross-selling, capture client flows and ensure transactions meet the Bank’s credit, legal, regulatory, operational and commercial objectives.
•
Monitor market developments across syndicated lending, private credit, structured finance, commodity finance, credit insurance and emerging-market fixed income, identifying trends that may affect investor appetite, pricing or transaction structures.
•
Represent the Bank with investors, clients and market participants at meetings, conferences and external forums, including acting as a public speaker, panellist or Bank representative when required and where significant travel may be necessary.

Qualifications
Qualification

Relevant degree, professional qualification or equivalent experience in banking, finance, capital markets, credit, structured finance, trade finance or a related discipline.
•
Fluency in written and spoken English is essential; fluency in one or more additional languages is desirable.
Experience
•
Minimum five years’ relevant experience in syndications, distribution, structured finance, commodity finance, private credit placement, emerging-market credit or a closely related role, preferably with direct emerging-markets exposure.
•
Demonstrable track record of distributing or placing trade finance, structured finance and commodity finance risk across bank, insurance, development finance and institutional investor channels.
•
Established access to buy-side investors and alternative capital providers, including private credit funds, asset managers, specialist trade and commodity funds, family offices and insurance investors.
•
Strong technical knowledge of trade-finance products, primary loan syndication, funded and unfunded participations, assignments, secondary loan sales, credit insurance and banking operations.
•
Strong understanding of credit risk, transaction structuring, risk allocation, pricing, investor requirements and the full execution cycle from market sounding through to documentation, allocation and closing.
•
Able to evaluate complex emerging-market transactions and translate them into clear, credible investor propositions.
•
Entrepreneurial, commercially focused and proactive, with strong relationship-building, communication, presentation and stakeholder-management skills.
•
Highly organised and accountable, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple workstreams under pressure and within tight deadlines.

Desirable experience includes local-currency emerging-market investment, portfolio or structured credit distribution, relationships with DFIs, MDBs, ECAs, sovereign or specialist investors, and development of new investor channels or distribution capabilities.

About This Job
Turner & Townsend is a global professional services company with over 10,000 people in 50 countries. Collaborating with our clients across real estate, infrastructure and natural resources sectors, we specialise in major programmes, programme management, cost and commercial management, net zero and digital solutions.
We are passionate about making the difference, transforming performance for a green, inclusive and productive world.
As well as helping organisations deliver and integrate new assets as quickly and efficiently as possible, we help set the asset strategies that support their corporate objectives. We also work with our clients to create safe and comfortable environments which are inexpensive to maintain, sustainable and practical to conduct business from.
OUR CORE VALUES
• We love a challenge
• We are stronger together
• We bring out the best in everyone
To support and progress our values, we:
• Developed a market leading suite of bespoke digital tools to deliver our market leading cost management services: The Hive
• Are a champion of a diverse workforce and culture
• Offer role development and advancement opportunities
• Set out our NewLeaf strategy, commitment to social value and environmental issues
• Provide opportunities for professional development (working with industry leading professionals, RICS Chartership development support, NEC accreditation)
• Offer a level of independence with multidisciplinary collaboration and support where needed
We want our people to succeed both in work and life. To support this we promote a healthy, productive and flexible working environment that respects work-life balance. We believe that everyone should pursue their passions and provide a real opportunity for this; whether you join one of our sports teams, social networks or bring a new interest to your colleagues.
MAIN PURPOSE OF ROLE
• To perform the role of the Commission Manager, taking responsibility for end-to-end service delivery
• To ensure that client objectives are met through the delivery of an effective cost management service
SCOPE
Senior Cost Managers handle commissions of varying sizes, depending upon the complexity of the project. Typically, projects fall within the £10m to £50m range.
KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES
Commission Management, to include:
• Coaching junior staff, including allocating roles and responsibilities to ensure effective cost management on all projects
• Advising clients on feasibility studies
• Advising clients on their procurement options
• Managing the estimating and cost planning stages, including presenting the final cost plan to the client
• Tendering and procuring, including managing the pre-qualification stage, producing the tender list, producing the preliminaries, tender analysis, producing the tender report and compiling the contractual documents, utilising the relevant cost management tools and services; The Hive; eTender Platform
• Conducting the role of contract administrator, including dealing effectively with post contract cost variances and the change control processes, where applicable referring major changes to line manager
• Taking personal responsibility for peer reviewing cost allowances and carrying out valuations on larger projects and in all cases ensuring that timely and accurate cost checking and valuation takes place
• Producing monthly post contract cost reports via our Cost Control App and presenting them to the client
• Inputting into value engineering
• Negotiating and agreeing final accounts
• Interfacing with the client, Project Manager, and other consultants, at all project stages
• Work collaboratively with Turner and Townsend’s project management team during project delivery
• Where appropriate, leading a cost management team, ensuring that they deliver on all of the above accountabilities
• Utilising our full suite of bespoke digital cost management tools and services; The Hive: Benchmarking App, CostX, Market Rates App, eTender Platform, and Cost Control App
• Implementing our Embodied Carbon Calculator, a bespoke carbon accounting tool, to produce carbon footprint reports
• Supporting the execution of our NewLeaf strategy
• Management of internal fees, internal job costing and resourcing requirements
Marketing and business development, to include:
• Identifying opportunities to develop new business with existing clients and reporting such opportunities to the appropriate line manager and by making effective use of the marketing database
• Developing and maintaining a professional network of peers and potential clients
• Leading bid submissions
• Identifying ways in which cost management procedures, templates and products can be improved
• Being involved in extracurricular activities including external groups, attending networking and CPD events
Internal management accountabilities, to include:
• Knowledge management – Ensuring that key information and learning generated from each commission is input into the Turner & Townsend internal database
• Process improvement – Identifying ways in which internal systems and processes can be improved and referring ideas to the appropriate line manager
• Lead in the support, development, and mentorship of junior staff members

Wise Assets is an investment product that allows eligible customers to earn a return on their money by investing it in the market rather than holding it as cash. It is a self-directed feature within the Wise multi-currency account where funds are placed into money market funds or stocks managed by third-party fund managers.

You will partner with the Head of Risk Product Governance and the wider Risk organisation to strengthen and continuously evolve the risk management programme supporting Wise Assets.
You will help ensure that risk frameworks are effectively embedded into the product lifecycle, operational processes, and strategic decision-making, while enabling Wise Assets to scale responsibly across multiple jurisdictions.
You will provide independent challenge, oversight and guidance to ensure risks are identified early, appropriately assessed, transparently reported, and effectively managed through enhancements to the control environment.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
•
Implement and embed Wise’s Enterprise Risk Management Framework (ERMF), associated policies, standards and methodologies across the Wise Assets product ecosystem, ensuring alignment with product developments and appropriate prioritisation of regulatory requirements. This will include establishing and maintaining risk appetite for Assets.
•
Partner with first line teams and co-ordinate with regional risk colleagues to ensure risk management practices are consistently applied and operating effectively across product, operational and governance processes.
•

About This Job
The main challenge now is to build a scalable architecture, meaning we have to tackle the challenges that come with using Python for distributed systems; Consistency, availability, service orchestration and much more.
We currently run different services, all with their own CI flows, allowing us to deploy several times a day.
In this role you will join a small, lean team of software engineers and a product manager working on;
• Building the integrated payment and checkout system using Python as well as the latest tools, technologies and methodologies.
• Supporting partner integration teams and ensuring that integration with partner retail checkout systems and API’s is easy and effortless
• Integrations with 3rd party payment systems such as (Stripe, Klarna, Apple Pay etc)
• A secure data management and CRM system for internal and external stakeholders (owasps etc)
• New ways to automate onboarding for retailers that allows for global regulations.
HOW WE WORK
We are developing an environment and culture that is all about writing great software using the best tools in the best possible manner.
We like to build things that solve problems, you will not be constrained by process - we work in small product teams that take a lean approach to building things.

Qualifications
In this team we’re looking for engineers who are excited to work on secure technologies in a python environment. You will ideally have plenty of experience using;
• Python, postgresql, jenkins, circleci, aws, redshift, redis, django, rest framework...
• Docker (http://developers.lyst.com/devops/2014/12/08/docker)
• Microservices architecture (HTTP)
• TDD - We love tests!
• We are using both Kanban and Scrum, depending if team is more customer facing or internal (Jira)

Additional Information
You will be challenged, supported and have the opportunity to learn a lot. You will work a fast paced, autonomous environment with like minded people who are passionate about what they do:
• 50 engineers and data scientists
• 5M duplicated products detected and merged using product image features (http://www.slideshare.net/ejlbell/fashion-productdeduplication)
• 300k online recommendation model updates per day (http://developers.lyst.com/data/2014/11/11/word-embeddings-for-fashion/)

• 40k product gender classifications per day via deep learning
• 500k recommended products per day
• 120 EC2, 8 RDS, 7 ElastiCache and 10 Redshift instances
• our internal analytics system collects ~100M data points/day
...and a team that…
• ~10 deployments/day
• 40+ merged pull requests/day
• 20k lines of change/week
• Lots of open source projects - https://github.com/lyst and https://github.com/SSAW
• Get invited to talk at great events (PyCon, Europython, PyData etc)
• feature toggling and A/B testing

Client-facing role responsible for driving revenue for the Global Markets desk, with a strong focus on derivatives, including swaps and forwards, and money market products. Qualifications
Qualifications

We are seeking a motivated and commercially minded Surveyor to join our Rating team. The successful candidate will provide professional advice on business rates for a diverse portfolio of commercial properties, helping clients minimise liabilities, manage risk, and navigate the UK rating system.
The role offers exposure to a wide range of sectors including office, industrial, retail, leisure, logistics, and mixed-use developments, working with both occupiers and investors.

• Manage a portfolio of commercial rating instructions across multiple property sectors.
• Prepare, review, and submit business rates appeals and proposals.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
• Ability to interpret market evidence and valuation information.
• Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
Desirable

• Experience of negotiating rating appeals with the VOA.
• Knowledge of the Check, Challenge, Appeal process.
• Familiarity with property databases and rating software.
• Existing client relationships or business development experience.

• Commercially aware with strong attention to detail.
