About This Job
Please note: Applicants should be UK based and already have the right to work here.
To deliver end-to-end grid connection process for the UK Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) portfolio, with additional support to global offshore wind as required. The role will focus on managing grid connection applications, Grid Connection Offers, coordinating technical studies, and ensuring compliance with G99 and Grid Code requirements. The Grid Manager will interface with internal teams, including development, construction, and procurement as well as external stakeholders such as DNOs, Transmission Owners (TOs), NGESO, Ofgem, and technical consultants.
This position offers hands-on experience across grid connection contracts, power system studies, and regulatory engagement, contributing to the successful delivery of strategic energy infrastructure projects.
Responsibilities
BESS Grid Connection Management
Development
• Support BESS projects from early development by providing grid-related expertise. Analyse connection options, costs, and programme impacts, advising on technical and commercial implications. Review connection offers, identify reinforcement schemes, and project-specific requirements.
• Review curtailment studies and provide grid and power system insights to support commercial business case development.
• Maintain clear communication across stakeholders, ensuring grid risks and opportunities are well understood.
Construction
• Work closely with the construction team in the electrical system design and grid integration of the project. Ensure the power system design complies with the grid requirements and the connection agreement. Ensure the requirements are clear to the contractors and internal teams.
• Review Grid compliance study reports and grid compliance test results. Be the main point of contact and manage the interface with the grid.
• Manage Power System data and modelling of the BESS assets. Manage Contractors and Power System consultants to deliver the reports on time and in quality.
• Liaise with DNO/TO/NESO regarding the grid compliance process.
Industry Engagement
• Participate in grid-related industry forums, working groups and consultations to contribute ideas, stay informed on emerging best practices, and represent the organisation’s interests in the evolving energy landscape.
Strategic Grid Planning & Policy Monitoring
• Support the tracking and interpretation of key policy and regulatory developments such as the Grid Connection Reform and the Review of Electricity Market Arrangements (REMA) to identify potential impacts and opportunities.
• Assist in tracking and interpreting changes to transmission planning methodologies and strategic frameworks including the Transitional Centralised Strategic Network Plan (tCSNP), Strategic Spatial Energy Plan (SSEP), Future Energy Scenarios (FES), and Clean Power 2030 (CP2030) to inform project development and stakeholder engagement strategies.
Offshore Wind Grid support
• Engage and maintain effective interfaces and collaborative relationships with the counter parts in our partner organisations.
• Support the wider Offshore team in the Due Diligence activities.
• Support our JV partners regarding the grid connection processes from initial assessment to final agreement.
Manage sub-contractors, vendors and suppliers
• Support and manage external consultants for any grid related work.
• Develop and maintain a network of stakeholders and explore collaborations.
Risk management, project governance and quality assurance
• Keep control of associated grid costs and charges such as fees or payment of security statements bi-annually to NGESO and provide input to the financial modelling of the project.
• Contribute to the establishment of effective grid connection management governance processes and systems to ensure internal efficiency and compliance with external grid management frameworks
• Ensure compliance with any relevant delegation of authority, cost and invoice management, risk management, human capital management, procurement management and others.

Qualifications
Preferred Qualifications:
• Masters’s degree in Electrical Engineering or any other related field
Preferred Experience:
• At least 5 to 7 years of experience in the power generation/distribution/transmission industry.
• Experience in successfully completing Grid Connection and Compliance of renewable energy assets.
• Experience in management and commercial understanding of the UK Grid market with expertise in DNO connections.
• Experience of development and execution of large-scale infrastructure projects.
Job-Specific Skills:
• In depth knowledge of grid connection process at distribution and transmission voltages of the BESS and renewable energy sector.
• Solid understanding of the key concepts, regulation and stakeholders of the UK Distribution & Transmission System and associated processes.
• Solid understanding of the Power system analysis and capabilities of various tools needed to perform the rating and performance studies.
• Experience in performing studies in RMS and EMT tools, and capability to perform them in house if needed - Load Flow, short circuit, harmonic, flicker, insultation coordination, G99/Grid Code compliance.
• Ability to review power system analysis reports and test results delivered by consultants (FAT/SAT) to identify any issues in the modelling and control system of the assets.
• Familiar with various BESS OEMs and BOP contractors and their capabilities.
• Proactive self-starter committed to adhere to a safe working environment.
• Exceptional communication skills and ability to work in a dynamic fast paced and diverse environment.
• Advanced project management and negotiation skills to persuade and influence decision makers to deliver relevant solutions for the business.
• Contract administration and legal skills.

Additional Information
Job-Specific Skills:
• Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills leading to a consultative approach within a corporate/multifunctional environment.
• Ability to manage cross-functional teams.
• Knowledge of the traditional energy industry.
• Project administration and legal knowledge.
• Project management skills and planning and organising.
• Attention to detail.
• Proven ability to manage and prioritize multiple ongoing projects acumen
As part of the application process, we will collect, store and process personal information about you.
Masdar will use your personal information in accordance with our Candidate Privacy Notice, which provides details on the purposes for which your data is processed.

Ready for a challenge?
Then Just Eat Takeaway.com might be the place for you. We’re a leading global online delivery platform, and our vision is to empower everyday convenience.
Whether it’s a Friday-night feast, a post-gym poke bowl, or grabbing some groceries, our tech platform connects tens of millions of customers with hundreds of thousands of restaurant, grocery and convenience partners across the globe.
About this role
Our logistics network spans 16 markets, hundreds of thousands of couriers and more than 350 million orders a year. Behind every order are real-time decisions: who delivers it, when, and at what price. Models running in production make them.
We are looking for a Director of Data Science & Machine Learning to lead the function behind those decisions and take the optimisation of our network to the next level. This is a leader-of-leaders role: a global team of 90+ data scientists, operations research scientists, ML engineers and MLOps engineers, led through managers and principal data scientists. You will set the DS/OR/ML agenda, not just run it.
The challenge is dual: keeping the real-time decision systems reliable at marketplace scale, while pushing the frontier on optimisation, supply/demand shaping and applied AI.
Location: Hybrid, 3 days a week from our London or Amsterdam office and 2 days working from home
These are some of the key components to the position:
• Deliver measurable improvement in delivery time, courier utilisation, cost per order, and the efficiency of courier pay.
• Own the strategy and roadmap for real-time decision systems: demand forecasting and supply balancing, order-to-courier assignment, and dynamic pay and fee pricing. All running as low latency production services at marketplace scale.
• Understand and shape courier behaviour: lead incentive and pay design grounded in economics and causal modelling, anticipating how couriers respond to the levers we pull
• Set the Operations Research agenda: combinatorial optimisation, exact and heuristic solvers, and simulation for capacity planning and policy testing
• Set the bar for validation before launch: backtesting and simulation frameworks that gate models going into production
• Own the quality of the ML platform and MLOps standards: feature and model pipelines, CI/CD, online and batch serving, monitoring and drift detection
• Drive experimentation and causal inference in a marketplace, including switchback and geo-based designs where network effects break standard A/B tests, and connect short-term experiment results to long-term outcomes such as courier retention and network health
• Build applied AI that delivers value in production, including LLM-based and agentic products for couriers and operations
• Build the organisation: hire, develop managers and principals, and build university partnerships
• Partner with Logistics Product, Logistics Engineering, Commercial and central Technology on production delivery of dispatch, estimations, pay, and supply/demand shaping actions, aligning on priorities and outcomes
What will you bring to the team?
• Leadership experience in Data Science, ML or Operations Research, including significant experience leading large organisations through managers across time zones, and developing those managers
• Deep credibility in real-time ML and marketplace or network optimisation (logistics, ride-hailing, delivery or similar)
• Experience taking models from research into low-latency production at scale
• Strong grounding in experimentation and causal inference under network effects, and in the economics of multi-sided marketplaces where participants respond strategically
• Excellent stakeholder management and communication, able to influence at the Product and Engineering leadership table and translate technical choices into business outcomes
• A pragmatic approach to AI: you ship value, not demos
• Advanced degree in a quantitative field (or equivalent experience)
At JET, this is how we play
Our teams forge connections internally and work with some of the best-known brands on the planet, giving us truly international impact in a dynamic environment.
Being the best at what we do isn’t just about delivering on our strategy. It's a competition for something incredibly valuable – our customers' choice. Every time a customer decides where to order, they're picking a side.
At the heart of the JET Customer League are our values and behaviours. They guide every interaction, every decision, every innovation. These are the actions we need to perform consistently and brilliantly, to surpass the competition and earn our customers’ loyalty, again and again.
Fun, fast-paced and supportive, the JET culture is about movement, growth, helping one another to succeed and celebrating wins. By truly living our values and embodying our behaviours, we’re building a customer-first culture which enables us to stay one step ahead of the competition.
Inclusion, Diversity & Belonging
No matter who you are, what you look like, who you love, or where you are from, you can find your place at Just Eat Takeaway.com. We’re committed to creating an inclusive culture, encouraging diversity of people and thinking, in which all employees feel they truly belong and can bring their most colourful selves to work every day.

Role Summary and Purpose
Arch Insurance is seeking a Data Platform Project Manager to lead delivery of a multi year data platform project. This project is replacing the legacy Enterprise Data Warehouse (EDW) and siloed data solutions with a modern, modular Enterprise Data Platform, supporting trusted reporting, business-aligned dashboards, self-service analytics and critical data feeds. The role will work across multiple functions including underwriting, operations, claims, IT and Finance to deliver data capabilities aligned to business priorities.
The successful candidate must have experience delivering complex data warehouse and data platform projects, together with London Market insurance experience. They must understand and articulate the value data platforms deliver to insurance companies, including trusted underwriting and financial insight, improved data quality and accessibility, operational efficiency and regulatory reporting. Proven experience managing multiple concurrent workstreams and multiple vendors or delivery partners is essential.
The role has no direct line management responsibility but requires leadership of multidisciplinary internal teams and external delivery partners. The Data Platform Project Manager will maintain an integrated delivery plan, manage cross-workstream dependencies and vendor commitments, and lead delivery from inception through testing, release, business adoption and transition to business-as-usual. Title:
Principal Technical Consultant – Asset Integrity & Asset Management
KBR is a global provider of differentiated, professional services and technologies delivered across a wide government, defense and industrial base. Drawing from its rich 100-year history and culture of innovation and mission focus, KBR creates sustainable value by combining engineering, technical and scientific expertise with its full life cycle capabilities to help our clients meet their most pressing challenges today and into the future.
We deliver science, technology and engineering solutions to governments and companies around the world. KBR employs approximately 37,000 people worldwide with customers in more than 80 countries and operations in over 29 countries. KBR is proud to work with its customers across the globe to provide technology, value-added services, and long-term operations and maintenance services to ensure consistent delivery with predictable results. At KBR, We Deliver.
KBR Consulting is seeking a Principal Consultant with asset integrity, life extension, and asset management consulting experience to join our international consulting organisation.
The successful candidate will be a senior technical leader, providing high-value advisory and practical engineering input across the full asset lifecycle, helping clients manage asset integrity and risk, improve reliability, and optimise performance.
KBR’s asset management services are built on decades of engineering knowledge across upstream, midstream, downstream, and petrochemical processes and equipment, with a proven track record as a business partner for operating companies and a practical owner-user perspective for right-sized solutions. This role will draw on KBR’s depth of resources, methodologies and tools across the wider business when needed.
Reporting to the KBR Consulting International leadership team, the Principal Consultant will deliver technically robust, commercially informed consulting assignments. Assignments typically include life extension evaluations, integrity and inspection programme assessments, maintenance planning, Reliability Availability & Maintainability (RAM) studies, risk, Health, Safety, Security & Environment (HSSE) / Process Safety Management (PSM) support, turnaround optimisation, and brownfield performance improvement, as well as technical due diligence and lender’s technical advisor engagements.
As a more experienced team member, the Principal Consultant performs their own work in terms of collecting information, developing deliverables, analysing trends and key findings, and preparing reports and presentations. Recognising their project management responsibilities, the Principal Consultant should have excellent organisational skills, be good at communicating and guiding others and adept at managing competing drivers often managing multiple assignments concurrently.
Additionally, the Principal Consultant will support the group’s overall sales effort through proposal/tender preparation, contract negotiation, and other client interfacing activities.
Key Responsibilities
Act as a technical authority on asset integrity management and structural/mechanical life extension, including facilities, infrastructure and equipment in operating/brownfield environments.
Lead or provide senior technical oversight for:
•
Structured asset life extension evaluations, including HSE and business risk-based approaches.
•
Debottlenecking studies including identification of existing constraints in a logical, sequenced manner against client production objectives, ranging from least costly, easiest implementation to more involved and costly solutions.
•
Mechanical integrity and inspection program assessments / gap closure, including management systems, procedures, execution, documentation and training, and a multi‑year continuous improvement model.
•
Integrity Operating Window (IOW) / Damage mechanism reviews / Corrosion Control Document (CCD) program development or validation and equipment reliability reviews to control and monitor damage mechanisms; and or determine end of life.
•
Risk Based Inspection (RBI) program implementations.
•
Fitness-for-Service (FFS) evaluations (Per API 579) and assessment of pressure equipment damage (including use of Finite Element Analysis (FEA) where appropriate).
•
Perform fire damage assessments to evaluate inspection and repair requirements.
•
Equipment asset care strategies and life cycle analysis, and operator care / onstream monitoring programs. Develop and review high-quality technical deliverables including reports, presentations, models and decision support materials, applying engineering judgement to identify integrity threats, operational constraints, risk drivers, and value‑led intervention options.
Client Engagement & Advisory
Act as a trusted technical advisor to clients, communicating effectively at both technical and executive levels, translating complex engineering topics into clear, decision‑ready business insights.
Support client discussions and delivery across the four core asset management pillars:
•
Asset Integrity Management (life extension, Mechanical Integrity (MI), inspection strategies, FFS, IOW/CCD).
•
Risk Management (insurance / loss control advisory, Root Cause Failure Analysis (RCFA), HSSE / PSM programs).
•
Reliability Programs (criticality, RAM, FMEA, electrical infrastructure, machinery lifecycle).
•
Process Optimisation (risk registers, turnaround scope optimisation, debottlenecking, business processes).
Reliability, Risk & Operational Readiness
Provide senior consulting input to improve reliability and reduce business risk, including:
•
Criticality analysis (rotating machinery and static equipment);
•
RAM analysis, including operability assurance and sparing optimisation for new and existing units and utilities.
•
Troubleshooting equipment performance leveraging discipline Subject Matter Experts and applyig Root Cause Failure Analysis (RCFA) methodology where appropriate.
•
Failure Mode & Effect Analysis (FMEA) and failure mode reviews;
•
Electrical infrastructure support (preventive maintenance programs, power system modelling e.g., ETAP, and electrical asset life extension programs).
•
Static & rotating machinery design & life cycle management (Preventative Maintenance (PM) / Predictive Maintenance (PdM) programs, lubrication/vibration/operator care strategies).
Process Optimisation & Turnaround / Outage Support
Lead or contribute to performance improvement and brownfield optimisation, including:
•
Risk register development to evaluate business and safety risk and optimise CAPEX/maintenance spend.
•
Turnaround & planned outage support, including TAR strategy / interval definition, risk-based scope development and scope challenge processes, critical path definition / optimisation, preparedness reviews, and post-TAR lessons learned.
•
Process engineering optimisation, such as process modelling/optimisation, debottlenecking studies, Process Safety…

About Analog Devices
Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X.
Solutions and Tool Specialist – Functional Safety
About the Role
Safety-critical semiconductor products are growing across every market ADI serves. The Functional Safety Office (FSO) is a global team responsible for independent safety confirmation at the highest integrity levels per ISO 26262, and the tooling and infrastructure that supports that work needs to scale with the portfolio.
This role puts you at the center of that challenge. You will build reusable analysis infrastructure — starting with Medini Analyze component libraries — support the development of training content, and work across multiple product families and design types rather than being embedded in a single program. You will gain broad cross-portfolio exposure to how safety-critical semiconductor products are developed.
This role offers a structured path into functional safety — with mentoring from experienced Safety Specialists, progressive project exposure, and the opportunity to build the tooling infrastructure that shapes how safety engineering scales across ADI. You are not expected to arrive as a functional safety expert. You are expected to arrive as an engineer with a solid foundation in semiconductor product development or quality engineering who wants to build tools, tool interfaces, reusable assets and workflows that improve engineering execution.
Why This Team
The FSO operates as ADI's independent safety authority, working across business units and product families rather than within a single design group. The team is global and high-impact — the tooling and methods you help build here will be used across every safety-critical product ADI ships. You will gain exposure to a breadth of product architectures and safety challenges that few individual contributor roles in the industry offer.
Job Responsibilities:
Support, develop and maintain reusable component libraries in Medini Analyze for safety analysis (FMEDA, FTA, dependent failure analysis) across ADI product families, working alongside the FSO's Safety Specialists to ensure technical accuracy and standards compliance.
Work with the FSO team and BU teams to standardize analysis templates and modeling patterns, and translate product-family-specific safety architectures into reusable, parameterized components that improve consistency and reduce setup time for new assessments.
Support the development of role-based training content for common safety activities including FMEDA execution, safety case construction, and safety requirements writing.
Engage with tool vendors such as Synopsys-Ansys (Medini Analyze) on capability evaluation, feature requests, and user community activities.
Develop functional safety domain expertise through structured mentoring and progressive project exposure, contributing to confirmation reviews and safety assessments as competence develops.
Who You Will Work With:
Day-to-day: You will work alongside the FSO's Safety Specialists around the world, who provide technical direction and mentoring on safety analysis and Medini.
Across the FSO: You will collaborate with Functional Safety Managers and Safety Specialists globally to understand where enablement assets have the highest impact.
Engineering teams: You will work with Design Engineers across business units who are the consumers of the tools, templates, and training content you help build.
Tool vendors: You will participate in vendor engagements with Synopsys-Ansys (Medini Analyze) and others on tool capabilities and integration.
Required Qualifications:
• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
• 5+ years of experience in semiconductor design engineering, quality engineering, systems engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
• Solid understanding of semiconductor product development processes and lifecycle.
• Experience with structured analytical methods used in product development such as FMEA, design verification, characterization, simulation, or reliability analysis.
• Experience building reusable technical assets such as component libraries, parameterized templates, structured analysis workflows, or design tools.
• Strong technical communication skills with the ability to translate complex methods into clear, usable guidance for engineering teams.
• Self-directed work style suited to a globally distributed team spanning multiple countries and time zones.
• Willingness to travel approximately 10%, primarily to ADI sites in Europe and the US.
Preferred Qualifications:
• Experience with safety analysis methods specifically (FMEA, FMEDA, FTA) including failure mode identification and classification.
• Experience with Synopsys-Ansys Medini Analyze or comparable safety analysis tools (Isograph, ReliaSoft, APIS IQ, Safety Office).
• Familiarity with functional safety standards (ISO 26262, IEC 61508) at a conceptual level. Direct certification is not required.
• Experience developing training content, structured knowledge management systems, or technical curricula.
• Familiarity with automotive quality standards such as IATF 16949 or development process standards such as ASPICE.
Functional safety is one of the fastest-growing disciplines in semiconductor engineering, and this role gives you a structured way in — with mentoring, real project exposure, and the chance to build infrastructure that engineering teams across ADI rely on. If you've been looking for a role with more cross-portfolio visibility and a longer lever than single-program work, we'd like to hear from you.
For positions requiring access to technical data, Analog Devices, Inc. may have to obtain export  licensing approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce - Bureau of Industry and Security and/or the U.S. Department of State - Directorate of Defense Trade Controls.  As such, applicants for this position – except US Citizens, US Permanent Residents, and protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) – may have to go through an export licensing review process.

At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.
The Position
The Opportunity
Roche, one of the leading global pharmaceutical companies, is delighted to announce the opening of its 2027 internship scheme for UK PhD students to join the Biostatistics team within the Product Development Data Sciences and Analytics (PDD) department located in Welwyn Garden City, UK.
Our biostatistics interns will work full-time for 10 weeks (extendable to 12 weeks) at our Roche Welwyn site under the supervision of experienced statisticians and data scientists. Interns will work on theoretical or applied problems with direct relevance to Roche’s ongoing clinical drug development in therapeutic areas such as oncology, immunology, infectious diseases, ophthalmology, or neuroscience.
There will be opportunities to interact with Roche’s global network of over 600 statisticians and data scientists. In addition to engaging in an exciting research topic, interns will have the opportunity to experience first-hand the work of statisticians and data scientists within the pharmaceutical industry and see how they add value to clinical development plans. Interns will learn both new technical and non-technical skills highly relevant to their future careers. At the end of the internship, students will give a department-wide presentation on their research topic.
Who you are
Applicants must currently be registered on a UK PhD programme with a significant methodological focus on statistics or data science, alongside relevant research experience within areas such as biostatistics/epidemiologists, statistics or mathematics, ideally but not necessarily with experience in the health sector. Applicants are required to have successfully passed their initial annual PhD review (typically held at 10-15 months) and must not have completed their PhD viva voce before the application closing date.
Application Process
Applications close on Friday, 13 November 2026. The application process may be extended beyond this date but could close at any point after this time.
Phase I: CV and Cover Letter Review (Your cover letter should not exceed two pages.)
As part of your cover letter, Roche is keen to understand your motivation in applying for this position. Also please include the following information:
• An introduction about yourself, confirming your availability for the face-to-face interview.
• Information about your PhD programme, current PhD status and year, confirmation that you have passed the initial annual review, and the expected viva voce date/year.
• A list of methodological or applied projects you have worked on in your PhD thesis, master’s dissertation, substantial undergraduate projects or previous internships and extracurricular activities, highlighting those within the relevant areas listed in the Requirements section.
• An explanation of why you are interested in the Roche internship programme, highlighting any relevant experience with health & medicine, biology, clinical trials or other non-statistical topics relevant to Roche.
• A description of broad areas (and specific topics, if you have any) in which you would be interested in working during the internship.
• A description of any skills or experience you have relevant to the role, such as team-working, multidisciplinary communication skills, etc.
• An explanation of whether you are eligible to work in the UK, have any visa restrictions or considerations regarding the paid/unpaid pathway, etc.
As an appendix to your cover letter, you can optionally attach a deliverable about one methodological or applied research project you have worked on and (nearly) completed, such as a published paper, working paper, master’s dissertation, or project report.
Phase II: In-person interview: Applicants should be available for a face-to-face interview in Welwyn Garden City on Friday 5th February 2027.
Please note:  Unfortunately visa sponsorship is not available for this role. Candidates must already hold valid authorisation to work in the UK.
Remuneration
Roche offers a competitive salary to a limited number of interns, who would normally be expected to pause their PhD stipend. For applicants from PhD programmes in which internships are an integral part of their PhD training (e.g., via the "Leave to Work Away" route while remaining registered in their PhD programme and continuing to receive the PhD stipend) or for those with visa-related restrictions, Roche can offer an unpaid internship, with alternative support to be agreed on a case-by-case basis. Authorisation from the university will normally be required to confirm the arrangement of the internship.
Working Environment and Culture
Roche offers the excellent benefits you would expect from a blue-chip organisation. There is a fully equipped gym on-site, a library and information centre, and an active sports and social club. We also have a subsidised staff restaurant providing food to cater to every taste throughout the day. At the heart of the building is an informal meeting area known as ‘The Street,’ which features a coffee shop, snack machines and cashpoint. A second building on-site, called ‘The Hub,’ contains modern meeting rooms and conference facilities.
Roche promotes personal well-being and work-life balance; therefore, flexible working options will be considered for all roles at Roche UK. Roche is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment. We foster diversity, equity and inclusion to reflect the communities we serve. When addressing healthcare on a global scale, diversity is essential to success. We believe that inclusion is key to understanding people’s varied healthcare needs. Together, we embrace individuality and share a passion for exceptional care. Join Roche, where every voice matters.
Who we are
A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.
Let’s build a healthier future, together.

IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in established businesses.

You will use AI tools and work closely with engineering, design, compliance, legal, and marketing to define and deliver the savings and cards proposition. You’ll also work closely with the Lifecycle teams, as these products are designed to broaden IG’s customer base and connect saving, spending and investing into one client relationship. The team operates at the intersection of product craft and commercial ambition, focused on building experiences that make saving, spending and investing feel effortless for IG’s customers.
Your role in the Team’s Success:
This is a role for a Senior PM who is as comfortable defining the strategy as they are shipping against it, and who is excited by building something new. As Senior Product Manager for Savings & Cards, you will own the product vision and multi-quarter roadmap for IG’s move into everyday saving and spending, determining which problems are worth solving, setting direction, and driving execution end to end. This is a zero-to-one proposition, starting in the UK and designed to be built once for reuse in other markets. You will operate with a high degree of autonomy, navigate ambiguity, and make decisions that directly shape commercial outcomes. You will not be handed a brief. You will write it.
What you’ll do:
Product strategy and roadmap
• Own the product vision and multi-quarter roadmap for Savings & Cards, aligned to IG’s commercial objectives. Don’t just contribute to it, set it.

• Drive competitive intelligence and translate market insights into differentiated propositions, including how saving, spending and investing connect into one IG relationship.
• Shape the proposition from first launch (such as Cash ISA) through to the longer-term product line, sequencing what to deliver and when.
Discovery and delivery

Navigation Electronic Warfare Engineer - Summer Placement 2027
As a Navigation Electronic Warfare Engineer, you will support vital work ensuring that MBDA missiles are able to navigate effectively in the most challenging electronic warfare environments.
Salary: £25,420 (pro-rata)
Dynamic working: 5 days per week on-site due to workload classification and need for access to site test facilities
Security clearance: British Citizen or a Dual UK national with British citizenship.
Restrictions and/or limitations relating to nationality and/or rights to work may apply. As a minimum and after offer stage, all successful candidates will need to undergo HMG Basic Personnel Security Standard checks (BPSS), which are managed by the MBDA Personnel Security Team.
This role is scheduled to close for applications at midnight on Monday 4th January 2027 but may close earlier depending on application volumes.
What we can offer you:
• 10 week placement: Starting June 2027, that allows you to apply your university learning to real-world projects and technologies
• Perform well on your placement and you could secure a graduate role before your final year
• Pension: Maximum total (employer and employee) contribution of up to 14%
• Overtime: Opportunity for paid overtime
• Annual Leave: 5 days
• Facilities: Fantastic site facilities including subsidised meals, free car parking and much more…
The opportunity:
MBDA Missiles cannot complete their missions without critical Navigation Sensors on board, withstanding enemy interference and providing robust navigation data to guide the missile to the target. Your work will directly influence the design of real missiles, with frequent exposure to high-profile, fast-paced projects.
The Navigation Sensors Group are responsible for the design of the missile navigation subsystems, including identifying and testing equipment from specialist manufacturers – this includes GPS receivers, anti-jam equipment, and Inertial Measurement Units.
You can choose to be based at either our Stevenage or Bristol site. Over the course of your 10-week placement you’ll get involved in:
• Supporting tests and trials to evaluate and assess navigation equipment performance
• Hands-on research and design activities to develop the next generation of navigation equipment
• Monitoring supplier and technology developments and identifying future technologies
• Collaborating with suppliers and researchers for the development and maturation of new and emerging technology
• Investigating engineering problems and conducting rapid technical analyses
In this role, you’ll work in a varied and dynamic environment, including as part of an international team with our colleagues in MBDA France and the wider MBDA Group. You’ll work alongside other departments to increase your knowledge on the complexities of a missile, including datalinks, seekers and sensors, and work closely with Integration and System Validation teams.
The work is technically challenging, innovative and rewarding. You’ll be working alongside experienced engineers who will encourage and help you develop the skills required to be an effective Navigation Electronic Warfare
What we're looking for from you:
Current undergraduate working towards a degree in a Physics, Mathematics, Electronics, or Engineering discipline.

• undefined

• undefined

• Supporting root-cause analysis and implementing sustainable corrective actions.
• Reviewing and optimising maintenance routines to improve equipment reliability and performance.
• Working closely with Production colleagues to build strong relationships and minimise disruption to manufacturing.

• Experience maintaining high-speed converting, printing, packaging or similar multi-station production machinery.
• Strong mechanical and electrical engineering skills, with experience of servo motors, precision gearboxes, pneumatic actuators and electronic sensors.

• The ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, pneumatic diagrams and mechanical drawings.

• A strong focus on safety, quality and continuous improvement.
• A proactive approach to problem-solving, with the ability to identify the root cause of issues rather than simply fixing the immediate problem.

• Coordinate manufacturing IT requirements related to production lines, machine connectivity, SCADA and OT environments, PLCs, production data capture, traceability, weighing, labelling, scanning and line-side terminals.

Job Description:
NEW GROUND WON’T BREAK ITSELF.
Every day our teams help people in businesses and communities to do what is right and achieve their goals.
Our Modelling team supports clients with financial modelling across the whole umbrella of Advisory services, with four main focus areas:
• Transactions and fundraising – sell-side or buy-side modelling to tell the story of a business, quantify risks, opportunities, and returns, and support fundraising
• Strategic planning and decision support – modelling to support ongoing business planning and to quantify the impact of strategic and routine decisions on a company’s results
• Restructuring and insolvency – turnaround planning to rebuild lender confidence, short-term cash flow forecasting, and insolvency outcome analysis
• Funds and valuations – asset and fund models to support initial transactions and ongoing valuation and reporting requirements, with a particular focus on the infrastructure sector
Financial models underpin almost all business decisions and all corporate transactions. We build, review and amend models across all sectors, and our tools and analysis help our clients understand the impact of their decisions before they make them. Our priority is delivering tools that are easy to understand, as well as flexible and robust in the face of change. Most of our work is executed in Microsoft Excel, with some use of other programming languages. We work as part of the firm's wider modelling community, sharing knowledge and best practice with other modelling experts.
The Associate Directors in the team are responsible for leading the delivery of modelling assignments, and for executing work of the most complex nature. You will work closely with clients, supporting the partners, directors and other Advisory teams to plan and lead modelling assignments, and play a role in organising and developing the team and its pipeline of business. This rare opportunity presents great scope to develop yourself and your career as the team grows.
We’re happy to talk flexible working and consider reduced hours, we’ll support you to balance your work and life.

As an Associate Director within our team, you will:
• Run modelling assignments on a day-to-day basis and maintain strong client relationships
• Execute and review modelling work with a great degree of autonomy and expertise
• Plan and develop financial models and other tools for clients, or assist in their design and development
• Review financial models built by clients and their advisers and compile initial views and findings
• Update and run financial models to provide analysis to support the firm’s wider deliverables (e.g. in Valuations, Insolvency, or Forensics situations)
• Review the modelling work of team members, ensuring technical excellence and brand compliance, and giving appropriate guidance and feedback
• Understand the results of models and engage with clients and colleagues in meaningful dialogue about the implications
• Prepare model specification and user guide documents to a high standard, requiring minimal amendments by the partner/director
• Manage risk on modelling assignments, including drafting and reviewing engagement letters
• Lead the pursuit process for new opportunities, including understanding client requirements and drafting proposals
• Proactively contribute to the team’s marketing efforts, including attending networking events, preparing presentations and marketing collateral
• Contribute to reports being prepared by other Advisory teams (e.g. Due Diligence, Corporate Finance, Restructuring)
• Manage your time and that of the team and deliver work in line with agreed budgets, monitoring time and costs and advising the partner/director/client as appropriate
• Provide coaching and training to junior team members
• Contribute to the operational and interpersonal success of the team
Knowing you’re right for us
Joining us as an Associate Director, the minimum criteria you’ll need is to have:
• Experience in a directly comparable Big 4 or similar modelling team
• Currently holding a senior manager or equivalent grade
• Excellent Excel proficiency and familiarity with advanced techniques
• Strong understanding of modelling best practice ideas
• Highly numerate with strong communication skills
• Logical approach to problem-solving, attention to detail
• A track record of collaboration with clients and colleagues
• Strong accounting skills and understanding of cash and working capital cycles
• Educated to degree level or equivalent, preferably in a numerate degree
• ACA or CA qualified or equivalent
It would be great if you had some of the following skills, but don’t worry if you don’t tick every box, we’ll help you develop along the way.
• Experience of coaching and/or mentoring others
• Have a defined specialism in a relevant target industry sector, or modelling specialism such as operational change or restructuring, is desirable.
• Experience with VBA programming or PowerBI
• Experience of business development and relationship building
Knowing we’re right for you
Embracing uniqueness, the culture at Grant Thornton thrives on the contributions of all our people, we never settle for what is easy, we look beyond to deliver the right thing, for everyone.  Building an inclusive culture, where we value difference and respect our colleagues helps our people to perform at the best of their ability and realise their potential.
Our open and accessible culture means you’ll interact with leaders who are interested in you and everything you bring to our firm. The things that set you apart, we value them. That’s why we give you the freedom to bring your whole self to work and pursue your passions inside and outside of work.
Beyond the job
Life is more than work. The things you do, and the people you’re with outside of work matter, that’s why we’re happy to look at flexible working options for all our roles, and we’ll always do our best to keep your work and life in balance.
The impact you can make here will go far beyond your day job. From secondments, to fundraising for local charities, or investing in entrepreneurs in the developing world, you’ll be giving back to society. It’s that drive to do the right thing that runs through…

Job Title
Senior Product Manager - OTC Trading
Job Description
Location: London, UK (Hybrid: 3 days in office)
Employment type: Permanent, full time
So, who are we?
IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in established businesses.
The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the platform to define what comes next.
Join us at IG – the future gets built here.
Your Team:
This role sits within the Trading & Investments domain of the Product function, reporting into the Head of Product, Trading & Investments. The domain’s mission is to give every client the tools to trade, from first investment to multi-asset portfolio. You will use AI tools and work closely with engineering, design, dealing, compliance, legal, and marketing to define and deliver the OTC trading proposition and help expand it to other markets. The team operates at the intersection of product craft and commercial ambition, focused on building trading experiences that feel effortless for IG’s customers while keeping them safe, informed and in control.
Your role in the Team’s Success:
This is a role for a Senior PM who is as comfortable defining the strategy as they are shipping against it. As Senior Product Manager for OTC Trading, you will own the product vision and multi-quarter roadmap for IG’s leveraged derivatives offering: spread bets, CFDs, options and futures. You will determine which problems are worth solving, set direction, and drive execution end to end. You will operate with a high degree of autonomy, navigate ambiguity, and make decisions that directly shape commercial outcomes. You will not be handed a brief. You will write it.
IG is moving towards a single, modern trading platform across its markets. This is a chance to shape what OTC trading looks like on that platform: rapid, reliable, secure and intuitive, for clients ranging from first-time derivatives traders to experienced professionals.
What you’ll do:
Product strategy and roadmap
• Own the product vision and multi-quarter roadmap for OTC trading, aligned to IG’s commercial objectives. You will set that roadmap, not just contribute to it.
• Determine which problems are worth solving and why, before any solution work begins.
• Make strategic build vs buy vs partner decisions grounded in customer needs, commercial viability, and technical feasibility.
• Drive competitive intelligence and translate market insights into differentiated propositions across spread betting, CFDs, options and futures.
• Shape how the OTC proposition converges onto a single global platform, balancing local market needs with a consistent client experience.
Discovery and delivery
• Run discovery that goes beyond what customers say. Understand the motivations, friction points, and habits that drive or block trading behaviour.
• Use AI tools actively across your workflow: synthesising research, generating prototypes, accelerating delivery, and surfacing insights faster.
• Partner with engineering and design to scope, prioritise, and ship with quality and pace.
• Define success metrics and iterate relentlessly based on evidence.
Cross-functional leadership
• Influence stakeholders across product, engineering, dealing, legal, compliance, marketing, and senior leadership. You drive alignment up, down, and across the organisation.
• Work closely with Peer Product Managers leading the adjacent areas, as well as coordinate with teams across Core technology to help build scalable backend systems.
• Navigate regulatory requirements (including product governance and Consumer Duty) and translate compliance constraints into seamless customer experiences, including how risk, margin and leverage are presented to clients.
• Work comfortably with APIs, pricing and execution infrastructure, and platform integrations.
• Identify opportunities to optimise and present pricing it in ways that helps customers and business.
• Mentor and raise the bar for PMs around you.
What You'll Need:
• Five or more years shipping consumer-facing products in trading platforms, investment platforms, neobanks, fintech, or adjacent consumer financial services.
• Proven ability to own and drive product strategy. That means vision setting and direction, not just roadmap input.
• Deep curiosity about trader and investor behaviour. You understand what makes people start trading, stop, switch, or stay.
• AI-native working style: you already use AI tools (LLMs, prototyping tools, research synthesis, workflow automation) to move faster and think better.
• Comfortable with ambiguity. You can define the problem when the brief doesn’t exist yet.
• Obsession with customer experience. You sweat the details that make journeys feel effortless, including in complex, real-time trading interfaces.
• Regulatory intuition. You can navigate compliance without it becoming a blocker to great UX, and you are comfortable working in a heavily regulated, risk-sensitive product area.
• Evidence and data-driven. You define metrics, run experiments, and make calls based on what works.
• Strong stakeholder management. You influence without authority and drive alignment across complex organisations.
Desirable
• Direct experience with leveraged or derivative products (CFDs, spread betting, options, futures, FX) or active trading platforms.
• Experience building or launching AI-powered features in a consumer product.
• Worked on platform partnerships, broker integrations, or exchange infrastructure.
• Built products that serve both novice investors and sophisticated traders.
• Experience in fintech, financial services, or a similarly regulated industry.
• Exposure to multi-market or multi-regulator product environments.
The perks
It really is more than a job. We think like a start-up, but we deliver like a FTSE 100 — so the bar is high, and we won't pretend otherwise. We work hybrid, which means three days in the office. We’ll recognise your talent and make sure that you can still have a life – at work, and outside of it. Networks, committees, awards, sports and social clubs, mentorships, volunteering opportunities, extra time off… the list goes on.
• Competitive salary
• Flexible Benefits Package on top of your salary (12%)
• Private medical cover for you and your family
• Life insurance
• Contribution to gym memberships
• 25 Days holiday, with 1 additional day off to celebrate your Birthday & 2 additional days off a year for voluntary work (28 in total)
• The option to buy or sell holiday days
• A comprehensive global and local onboarding process
• Enhanced primary (maternity), secondary (paternity), and shared parental pay…

Discover your opportunity with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), one of the world’s leading financial groups. Join MUFG, where being inspired is expected and making a meaningful impact is rewarded.
Overview of the Department/Section
The Living Sector Finance team sits within the Structured Finance Office for EMEA and is responsible for the origination, structuring and execution of Real Estate Finance transactions across the UK and Europe.
The team provides financing solutions to institutional sponsors and financial institution clients, with a primary focus on the Living Sector. Core areas of coverage include Purpose-Built Student Accommodation (PBSA), Build-to-Rent (BtR) and Affordable Housing.
As part of MUFG's strategic growth ambitions within Real Estate Finance, the team is expanding its activities across both Living Sectors and Logistics. Logistics has been identified as a key strategic growth area for the Bank, creating an opportunity to broaden client coverage, develop sector expertise and establish a scalable lending franchise across the UK and Europe.
Working closely with Sponsor Coverage, Syndication, Credit, Legal and other product partners, the team originates and executes tailored financing solutions for clients whilst maintaining a strong focus on credit quality, risk management and long-term client relationships.
Team members are expected to play an active role in supporting business development, transaction origination, structuring and execution, whilst contributing to the continued growth of the Living Sector platform and the development of MUFG's Logistics strategy across EMEA.
Number of Direct Reports
N/A
Main Purpose of the Role
To support the continued growth of MUFG's Real Estate Finance business through the origination, structuring and execution of financing transactions across the Living Sector and Logistics. The role holder will be responsible for identifying and developing new business opportunities, leading transaction execution processes and managing internal approval requirements across a range of complex real estate financing transactions.
Working closely with Sponsor Coverage, Credit, Syndication, Risk Management, Legal and other internal stakeholders, the role holder will play a key role in delivering tailored financing solutions for institutional sponsors and financial institution clients across the UK and Europe.
A key aspect of the role will be supporting the development and implementation of MUFG's Logistics strategy, including building sector expertise, establishing lending parameters, securing internal approvals and originating new transaction opportunities.
Key Responsibilities
• Originate, structure and execute Real Estate Finance transactions across the Living Sector and Logistics sectors throughout the UK and Europe.
• Support the continued growth of MUFG's Living Sector franchise, with a focus on Purpose-Built Student Accommodation (PBSA), Build-to-Rent (BtR) and Affordable Housing.
• Play a key role in the development and implementation of MUFG's Logistics lending strategy, including supporting internal approvals, establishing sector expertise and originating new business opportunities.
• Identify, evaluate and pursue financing opportunities with institutional sponsors and financial institution clients.
• Lead transaction execution processes from origination through to financial close, coordinating internal and external stakeholders throughout the transaction lifecycle.
• Prepare and present high-quality credit applications, approval papers, committee materials and transaction recommendations.
• Undertake detailed financial analysis, cashflow modelling, transaction structuring and risk assessment to support lending decisions.

Job Description:
Start date: September 2027
Location: Broughton
Duration: 36 months

Salary: A competitive starting salary of £19,185
35 hours per week (on either a standard working day or a double-day shift pattern, providing flexibility) // 25 days holiday plus bank holidays // Pension // Success share // Plus many more flexible benefits!
About us:
Ready to build the wings that lift the world? Join Airbus as a Craft Machining Apprentice in Airbus Broughton and play a vital role in manufacturing wings for our A320, A330, and A350 aircraft families. This 36-month program offers valuable hands-on training, recognised qualifications, and a clear path to a rewarding career in aviation."
At Airbus, we believe a diverse workforce drives innovation. We're committed to fostering an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued and empowered to thrive.  Airbus is a global pioneer in the aerospace industry, leading the way in designing, manufacturing, and delivering aerospace products across Commercial Aircraft, Helicopters, Defence, and Space sectors. As the global center of excellence for wing manufacturing, our Broughton site delivers over 500 wing sets annually. Our apprenticeship programs are carefully designed to give you valuable practical training alongside your academic studies, setting you up for success and helping your career truly fly.
With over 17,5000 employees worldwide and as the largest aeronautics and space company in Europe, Airbus is at the forefront of the aviation industry. During your apprenticeship you will work alongside our experienced engineers and quality team to support you to complete the work safely and efficiently
What you will be doing:
As a Craft Machining Apprentice, you'll immerse yourself in hands-on technical experience in the workplace while completing your academic studies. This program is designed to equip you with valuable qualifications and competencies to work directly on live aircraft. You'll also benefit from our Gen A support network and learning HUB, providing additional support, events, and opportunities for all early career participants.
This 36-month apprenticeship is structured to maximise your learning and impact:
Year One: You will spend the first 12 months of your apprenticeship based at Coleg Cambria, Bersham Road, Wrexham, working towards obtaining:
• NVQ L2 diploma in Performing engineering operations
• City & Guild 2850 Level 2 In Machining
• Level 2 Essential Skills
This will allow you to develop the necessary skills, knowledge and experience to enable you to make an immediate contribution when you enter the workforce in the second year.
Year 2 and 3:  Your Learning Takes Flight at Broughton! Building on your foundational knowledge, you will be based at Airbus Broughton (North Wales) and you'll join our expert team of Machinists within the machine shop area, supporting the manufacture of wing skins, panels and stringers for various Airbus aircraft.  The tasks will be varied,  and will require you to apply your skills directly to live projects,  allowing you to work on the job whilst gaining the relevant skills, knowledge and experience. This will include:
• Carrying out a variety of different techniques including following bespoke set up sheet instructions to complete a machining process as well as the use of stringer machining and long bed milling machining practices within the Airbus Broughton plant, completing this to a high competent level and in a safe efficient manner.
• Through your training you will have the ability to demonstrate effective loading and locating of billets, and unloading of finished components within the Airbus Broughton plant, completing this to a high competent level and in a safe efficient manner.
Additionally you will also attend college on day release, working towards gaining:
• Level 3 Extended Diploma in Mechanical Manufacturing Engineering (Machining Bias Units)
• City & Guild 2850 Level 3 Machining
Upon successful completion of your 36-month apprenticeship, you'll become a skilled Machinist  working within the Large component manufacture (LCM) team supporting our world-class Airbus aircraft. You'll receive a Modern Apprenticeship Certificate, setting you up for a fantastic career.

In order to be eligible to this apprenticeship you must:
• Achieve a minimum of five GCSEs which must include:
• Grade C or 4 in Maths (GCSE certificate only - no equivalency accepted)
• Grade C or 4 in English Language (GCSE certificate only - no equivalency accepted)
• Grade CC or 44 in Double Award Science OR Grade C/4 in Single award in Physics.
• Plus 2 other GCSEs at grade C or 4 (other qualifications that are equivalent or higher may be considered as an alternative to the additional 2 GCSE’s, preferably in a practical or technical subject (e.g., Design & Technology, Engineering, etc)
• Attach your CV (stating your predicted or achieved grades) and cover letter stating your motivation for the role and industry.
To be a successful candidate you need to have a passion for learning, enjoy hands-on, teamwork and problem-solving activities.

What is it about Airbus that makes you excited to start a career with us? Is it our aircraft, innovation, global impact, or something else? Let us know what interests you about our work and why we stand out to you.
• Why a hands-on apprenticeship?
Why do you want to learn by doing? We’d love to hear what draws you to practical, skills-based learning.
• Show your hands-on experience.
In your CV or cover letter, include any hands-on activities or hobbies where you've used practical skills. These could be things like:
• DIY projects
• Building and fixing things
• Doing make-up or beauty work
• Tinkering and Tech Projects
• Building models
• Baking or cooking
• Others

GRADES: Any offer will be conditional upon us receiving evidence of your required grades 24h after receiving your certificates on results day, in addition to completing all pre-employment checks and online forms.

RIGHT TO WORK IN THE UK: Candidates must have current legal authorisation to work in the United Kingdom. For more information, please check the Government Website.

At Grant Thornton we do things differently - looking to the future, driving ambitious growth and pioneering positive change in our industry. Job Description:
Grant Thornton’s Alternative Funds tax team provides tax advisory, transactions and compliance services to alternative fund managers across all asset classes including private equity, venture capital, private debt, hedge funds, real estate and infrastructure.
The team’s client portfolio spans the breadth of the asset management sector, serving traditional asset managers, financial services institutions, private equity funds, alternative investors, the real estate sector, wealth and hedge asset managers, UK pension funds, and global institutional investors. We combine technical expertise with a commercial approach, to build a strong trusted adviser relationship with our clients.
The Alternative Funds tax team sits as part of the wider Financial Services Tax team, which provides tax services to a variety of clients in the Financial Services market across Wealth and Asset Management, Banking and Capital Market and Insurance sectors.
We have ambitious growth plans and are looking for an experienced, enthusiastic Associate Director with strong UK tax compliance and advisory experience to join our team in London. The alternative funds industry is dynamic, technically demanding and global, giving you the opportunity to work on domestic and international structuring, transactions and UK tax compliance and advisory matters, in addition to working with the wider Grant Thornton International network.
You will be responsible for managing the full suite of tax compliance and advisory services for asset managers themselves and the funds they manage, across the entire investment lifecycle including fund structuring, structuring carried interest arrangements, structuring the investment and divestment of assets and ongoing tax compliance and investor reporting.
Part of the role will focus on working alongside the partner group in building out the practice, building strong client relationships within the current and target client base. Working in practice means that the job is, by its nature, different every day and we want someone who is actively looking for this challenge. An agile approach to working with different projects and people is therefore essential.
We’re happy to talk flexible working and consider reduced hours and job shares, we’ll support you to balance your work and life.
A look into the role
As an Associate Director you will:
•
Take ownership of providing highly technical tax advice to asset managers and the funds they manage throughout the investment lifecycle of the fund, including transaction and tax structuring support
•
Deliver partnership tax and corporate tax compliance services to asset management businesses, ensuring their tax reporting obligations and compliance deadlines are met
•
Assist with investor reporting to enable clients to effectively communicate taxable results to their individual investors
•
Develop and lead your own diverse client portfolio, ensuring a high level of client service
•
Work closely with our colleagues cross the Grant Thornton’s tax practice, Financial Services Industry and international network to identify opportunities from both new and existing clients
•
Actively contribute to business development activities by proactively managing existing relationships and pitching work to new clients
•
Proactively train and develop more junior members of the team, including through the delivery of bespoke training sessions
•
Have a thorough understanding and adhere to the firm’s risk management and quality procedures
Knowing you’re right for us
Joining us as an Associate Director the minimum criteria you’ll need is a professional qualification (CTA / ACA / ACCA or equivalent), and to be confident managing a portfolio of clients.
It would be great if you also had some of the following skills, but don’t worry if you don’t tick every box, we’ll help you develop along the way.
•
Strong tax technical skills and an interest in the financial services sector (previous experience of working with one of the asset classes (private equity, venture capital, private credit) is preferred but is not essential
•
Mix of corporate and partnership tax compliance experience
•
A track record of leading projects, with a focus on accountability, high quality and timely delivery.
•
Self-motivated and strong team player.
•
Excellent interpersonal skills are required in addition to strong oral and written communication skills.
•
Familiarity with Alpha tax, CCH personal tax, Power BI, Microsoft Office, and other relevant software.
•
Experience of coaching and developing more junior team members.
Knowing we’re right for you
Embracing uniqueness, the culture at Grant Thornton thrives on the contributions of all our people, we never settle for what is easy, we look beyond to deliver the right thing, for everyone.  Building an inclusive culture, where we value difference and respect our colleagues helps our people to perform at the best of their ability and realise their potential.
Our open and accessible culture means you’ll interact with leaders who are interested in you and everything you bring to our firm. The things that set you apart, we value them. That’s why we give you the freedom to bring your whole self to work and pursue your passions inside and outside of work.
Beyond the job
Life is more than work. The things you do, and the people you’re with outside of work matter, that’s why we’re happy to look at flexible working options for all our roles, and we’ll always do our best to keep your work and life in balance.
The impact you can make here will go far beyond your day job. From secondments, to fundraising for local charities, or investing in entrepreneurs in the developing world, you’ll be giving back to society.  It’s that drive to do the right thing that runs through our every move, grounded in our firm’s values – purposefully driven, actively curious and candid but kind.
We’re looking for people who want to contribute, spark fresh ideas and go beyond expectations. People who want to be able to proudly do what’s right, for the firm, our clients, our people and themselves. It’s how it should be.

Volunteer "Reading Through Recovery" Group Facilitator
Location: Some flexibility depending on staff and volunteer availability and ability to travel though meetings are currently held in Weymouth, Dorchester and online.
Timing: We are looking for someone who can offer around 2-3  hours per week
About Waythrough
Waythrough provides specialist support across mental health, alcohol, drugs and related areas. We delivery high-quality, evidence-based services designed around the real needs of the people we serve.
Every year, we support around 125,000 people through over 250 services - and it's all made possible by our 3,500 brilliant staff and volunteers.
Make a real difference in your community
Are you passionate about helping others live safer, healthier, more independent lives? Join our team at Waythrough and support people facing challenges around mental health, substance use, housing or domestic abuse. This is more than just a job – it’s a chance to build meaningful relationships and create lasting change.
Reach Drug and Alcohol Services is the commissioned community drug and alcohol provision for Dorset. It provides a range of support, interventions and treatments for adults and young people wanting to make positive changes to their drug and/or alcohol use, as well as offering support to family members and running campaigns and events that raise awareness of addiction and celebrate recovery in the community.
Reading Through Recovery
A weekly 90‑minute group supporting anyone on a substance or alcohol recovery journey, whether actively using or abstinent, through the shared experience of reading.​
​
In a relaxed and inclusive space, participants bring a book they’re reading, explore themes that resonate, and dive into stories that spark insight and strength. Together, we share literature that has inspired, supported, or shaped our recovery journeys, with optional recommendations and themed reading ideas each week.​
​
This is more than a book group, it's a place to find meaning, connection, and momentum in recovery.​
Details of the role & tasks
The role:
We are seeking enthusiastic readers to co-facilitate our new project – Reading Through Recovery. Volunteer group facilitators will help to make newcomers feel welcome, and empower everyone in the meeting to contribute, should they wish to.
This role is ideally suited to people with lived experience of recovery, either directly, or through supporting a close friend or family member, although we welcome applications from anyone with an empathetic, non-judgemental attitude that can build strong working relationships with others.
Tasks may include:
• Facilitating a non-judgemental space to allow participants to express feelings and share experiences freely.
• Foster a sense of community and trust
• Enable participants to connect through shared narratives, enabling them to relate to one another’s journeys.
• Encourage reflection and discussion.
Personal qualities
Skills we would love you to bring to the role:
• Welcoming, friendly and an ability to put other people at ease
• Confident and calm in group settings
• Good IT skills – the SMART Recovery UK training all takes place electronically and includes submitting some written responses via email
• Non-judgmental towards people facing challenges in their lives, including around drug and/or alcohol use and/or mental health
• Good time keeping
• Able to work as part of a team, on own initiative and to instruction
• An understanding of Waythrough – information is available on our website
• A genuine interest in being part of the mission and vision of Waythrough
• Ability to maintain professional boundaries, adhere to Waythrough policies and media guidelines, engage in supervision, and complete relevant training
Training: Volunteers have access to Waythrough’s training platform, LearningKind, and will be asked to complete an induction workshop ahead of their start date and a number of training modules within their first 3 months.
What We Offer
We value the people who make a difference every day. Alongside meaningful work, you’ll enjoy:
•
Discounts from various schemes
•
Training and personal development
•
A chance to make a real difference in people’s lives
•
Free induction and role-specific training
•
Support from experienced staff and regular supervision
•
Opportunities to meet new people and develop your confidence
•
Reimbursement for travel and agreed expenses
•
Valuable experience that can support your personal or career development
